docs.title: MT4Account — Low-Level API (Layer 1 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT4Account is the thin, 1:1-with-the-wire layer. Every method maps to a single gRPC RPC: you pass a protobuf *Request and get back the protobuf *Data payload of the reply. It owns the gRPC channel, the service stubs, the connection/identity state and the transport machinery — transient-failure retry with exponential back-off and an automatic ConnectEx re-attach on TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND.

#include <metarpc/mt4_account.hpp>   // pulls in the generated protobuf headers

When to use this layer

Use MT4Account when you need a field the friendly layers do not expose, or full control over the exact request. For everyday work prefer MT4Service (friendly structs) or MT4Sugar (one-liners), which hide protobuf and compile fast.

Per-method deep dives

This page is the compact reference. For a detailed write-up of every method (signature, request/reply, input/output tables, enums, worked examples) see the MT4Account — Master Overview and its section pages.

docs.title: 🆚 MT4 vs MT5 (if you know the MT5 SDK)
docs.text:
• No "positions". There are only orders — openedOrders() returns market and pending orders in one list. Tickets are int32.
  • No DOM, no orderCalcMargin / orderCalcProfit / orderCheck. MT4 has no server-side pre-trade calculators.
  • Trades have no retcode. A rejected trade throws ApiError carrying the MQL4 error code (e.g. 132 market closed, 130 invalid stops) — there is no 10009-style status.
  • Timeframes are in MINUTES (M1=1, H1=60, D1=1440).
  • Every message carries both server time and a _utc field.

docs.title: How a call works
docs.text:
• Protobuf in, protobuf out. accountSummary() returns a pb::AccountSummaryData; you read fields with the generated accessors (.account_balance(), .account_login(), …).
  • No UTC conversion. Times are raw broker server time (plus a _utc field on each message). MT4Service is the layer that selects UTC for you.
  • Errors are exceptions (never error codes):
    • metarpc::ApiError — the gateway/terminal answered with an error payload (bad login, unknown symbol, trade rejected, …). Carries code, message, and the MQL4 code (mqlErrorCode).
    • metarpc::TransportError — a gRPC transport failure that outlived the retry budget.
  • Retry & reconnect are automatic (see ClientOptions). You do not retry yourself.
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt4_term_api;

MT4Account acc("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, /*apiKey*/ "");
acc.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

try {
    pb::AccountSummaryData s = acc.accountSummary();
    std::cout << s.account_login() << "  " << s.account_balance() << " " << s.account_currency() << "\n";
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    std::cerr << e.code << ": " << e.message << "\n";
}

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Every onX() opens a server stream and delivers raw protobuf payloads to your callback on a background thread. The returned AccountStream owns the subscription — keep it alive to keep receiving, destroy it (or call stop()) to cancel.

Method Callback payload onSymbolTick(req, cb) pb::OnSymbolTickData onTrade(req, cb) pb::OnTradeData onOpenedOrdersProfit(req, cb) pb::OnOpenedOrdersProfitData onOpenedOrdersTickets(req, cb) pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData onConnectState(req, cb) pb::ConnectStateData

AccountStream exposes stop(), running(), count(), lastError().

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req;
req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
auto stream = acc.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (d.has_symbol_tick())
        std::cout << d.symbol_tick().symbol() << " " << d.symbol_tick().bid() << "\n";
});
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
stream->stop();   // (also happens automatically when `stream` is destroyed)

docs.title: MT4Service — Friendly Facade (Layer 2 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT4Service is the mid-level layer: the same operations as MT4Account, but with plain arguments, clean C++ structs (no protobuf) and times in UTC. Its header is protobuf-free, so strategy code compiles fast.

#include <metarpc/mt4_service.hpp>   // no protobuf headers pulled in

Full write-up

This page is the compact reference. For the grouped deep-dive — every method's signature, return struct and a worked example — see the MT4Service — Overview and its section pages.

using namespace metarpc;

MT4Service svc("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);         // utcTimes defaults to true
svc.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

AccountInfo a = svc.accountSummary();
std::printf("Equity %.2f %s\n", a.equity, a.currency.c_str());

Each MT4Service owns one MT4Account; reach the raw layer via svc.account().

docs.title: MT4Sugar — One-Liner Helpers (Layer 3 of 3)
docs.text:
metarpc::MT4Sugar is the high-level layer: self-contained one-liners for everyday tasks — "what's my balance?", "buy 0.1 lots", "close everything". No context, no request objects, no protobuf. The header compiles fast.

#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>

Full write-up

This page is the compact reference. For grouped deep-dives with examples, see the MT4Sugar — Overview and its section pages.

Never throws on an ordinary rejection

A rejected trade throws ApiError from Layer 1; the sugar helpers catch it and report false / 0. Trading helpers return the ticket (0 on rejection); close/modify return bool.

using namespace metarpc;

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");   // or sugar.quickConnect() from env

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", /*risk%*/ 1.0, /*SL pips*/ 20);
int ticket  = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 20, 40);

Each MT4Sugar owns an MT4Service; reach it via sugar.service(), or the raw layer via sugar.account().

docs.title: ENUMs Usage Reference — CppMT4
docs.text: Every enumeration the CppMT4 API uses, with exact values and where it appears. The protobuf enums are generated into the mt4_term_api namespace (namespace pb = mt4_term_api;); the friendly MT4Service layer exposes enum class mirrors.

docs.title: How enums work here
docs.text:
protobuf's C++ codegen puts enum values at namespace scope — they are not enum class. You write the bare constant and compare it directly:

namespace pb = mt4_term_api;

pb::OpenedOrdersRequest req;
req.set_sort_type(pb::SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC);          // just the value

pb::AccountSummaryData a = account.accountSummary();
if (a.account_trade_mode() == pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL) { /* ... */ }

The friendly layer uses typed enum class instead: TradeMode, OrderType, Timeframe — e.g. svc.bars(sym, Timeframe::H1, from, to).

⚠️ Three order-type enums, same six values. OO_OP_* when reading orders (OpenedOrderType), OC_OP_* when sending (OrderSendOperationType), SUB_OP_* in stream frames (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE). Don't mix the prefixes.

docs.title: 1. EnumAccountTradeMode — account type
docs.text:
Used by: accountSummary → AccountSummaryData.account_trade_mode().

Value Int Meaning pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO 0 Demo account pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST 1 Contest account pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL 2 Live account

Friendly mirror: metarpc::TradeMode { Demo, Contest, Real } on AccountInfo::tradeMode.

if (account.accountSummary().account_trade_mode() == pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL)
    std::puts("LIVE account — be careful");

docs.title: 2. EnumAccountMarginMode — margin calculation mode
docs.text:
Used by: accountSummary → AccountSummaryData.account_margin_mode().

Value Int Meaning pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING 0 Netting (parity with MT5) pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE 1 Exchange pb::ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING 2 Hedging — typical MT4

MT4 is hedging (several orders per symbol). The other values exist for parity with MT5.

docs.text:
Used by: openedOrders → OpenedOrdersRequest.sort_type.

Value Int pb::SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC 0 pb::SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC 1 pb::SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC 2 pb::SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC 3

docs.title: 4. EnumOrderHistorySortType — history sort
docs.text:
Used by: ordersHistory → OrdersHistoryRequest.input_sort_mode.

Value Int pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC 0 pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC 1 pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC 2 pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC 3 pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC 4 pb::HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC 5

docs.text:
Used by: quoteHistory → QuoteHistoryRequest.timeframe.

Value Int Period pb::QH_PERIOD_M1 0 1 minute pb::QH_PERIOD_M5 1 5 minutes pb::QH_PERIOD_M15 2 15 minutes pb::QH_PERIOD_M30 3 30 minutes pb::QH_PERIOD_H1 4 1 hour pb::QH_PERIOD_H4 5 4 hours pb::QH_PERIOD_D1 6 1 day pb::QH_PERIOD_W1 7 1 week pb::QH_PERIOD_MN1 8 1 month

Used by: bars → QuoteHistoryBarsRequest.timeframe. This is the scheme the friendly Timeframe enum mirrors.

Value Int Friendly pb::QHB_PERIOD_M1 1 Timeframe::M1 pb::QHB_PERIOD_M5 5 Timeframe::M5 pb::QHB_PERIOD_M15 15 Timeframe::M15 pb::QHB_PERIOD_M30 30 Timeframe::M30 pb::QHB_PERIOD_H1 60 Timeframe::H1 pb::QHB_PERIOD_H4 240 Timeframe::H4 pb::QHB_PERIOD_D1 1440 Timeframe::D1 pb::QHB_PERIOD_W1 10080 Timeframe::W1 pb::QHB_PERIOD_MN1 43200 Timeframe::MN1

docs.title: 6. OrderSendOperationType — order type (requests)
docs.text:
Used by: orderSend → OrderSendRequest.operation_type.

Value Int Meaning pb::OC_OP_BUY 0 Market buy pb::OC_OP_SELL 1 Market sell pb::OC_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit pb::OC_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit pb::OC_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop pb::OC_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop

Same numbering as MQL4 OP_BUY..OP_SELLSTOP. Friendly mirror: OrderType on OrderRequest::type.

docs.title: 7. OpenedOrderType — order type (reads)
docs.text:
Used by: openedOrders / ordersHistory → OpenedOrderInfo.order_type() / HistoryOrderInfo.order_type().

Value Int Meaning pb::OO_OP_BUY … pb::OO_OP_SELLSTOP 0–5 market / pending (as above) pb::OO_OP_BALANCE 6 Balance entry (history only — not a trade) pb::OO_OP_CREDIT 7 Credit entry (history only — not a trade)

Friendly mirror: OrderType { Buy, Sell, BuyLimit, SellLimit, BuyStop, SellStop, Balance, Credit } with Order::isPending() / isBuy().

docs.title: 8. OrderCloseDeleteMode — what a close/delete did (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: orderCloseDelete → OrderCloseDeleteData.mode().

Value Int Meaning pb::OCD_MARKET_ORDER 0 A market order was closed pb::OCD_PENDING_ORDER 1 A pending order was deleted

docs.title: 9. SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE — where the UTC offset came from (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: serverTimezone → ServerTimezoneData.source().

Value Int Meaning pb::SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_UNKNOWN 0 Not read yet; utc_offset_seconds stays unset pb::SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LIVE 1 Read live by this terminal pb::SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE_LAST_VALIDATED 2 Last validated offset for this broker

docs.title: 10. MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE — streaming event group (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: onTrade → OnTradeData.type(); onOpenedOrdersProfit → OnOpenedOrdersProfitData.type().

Value Int pb::OrderProfit 0 pb::OrderUpdate 1

docs.title: 11. SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE — order type in stream frames (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: onTrade / onOpenedOrdersProfit order rows → .type() (OnTradeOrderInfo, OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo).

Value Int Meaning pb::SUB_OP_BUY … pb::SUB_OP_SELLSTOP 0–5 Buy / Sell / *Limit / *Stop

docs.text: Three enums describe a symbol's trading rules, on SymbolParamsManyInfo (from symbolParamsMany).

Note the proto typo MARGINE (not MARGIN) — frozen into the contract.

Value Int Meaning pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED 0 Trading disabled pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_LONGONLY 1 Long only pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_SHORTONLY 2 Short only pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_CLOSEONLY 3 Close only pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL 4 Full access

docs.text:
Used by: SymbolParamsManyInfo.tradeexemode().

Value Int Meaning pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_REQUEST 0 Request execution pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_INSTANT 1 Instant execution pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET 2 Market execution pb::SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_EXCHANGE 3 Exchange execution

docs.title: Not passed as values, but you'll meet them
docs.text:
• MqlErrorCode — the MQL4 trade-error numbers (0, 130, 132, …) that arrive in ApiError::mqlErrorCode. Full table in Return Codes.
  • ErrorType — the gateway Error payload's category (type field), folded into ApiError for you.

Other enums in the generated pool (ChartTemplateMode, EA_PARAM_TYPE, GuiFormFieldType, LogType, TerminalType, ProxyTypes, …) belong to admin / GUI / charting RPCs that the trading SDK (MT4Account / MT4Service / MT4Sugar) does not surface.

See also: MT4Account — Master Overview · SymbolParamsMany · Return Codes · MT4Service API

docs.title: Getting Started with CppMT4
docs.text: Quick Setup & Overview — start automating your trading with CppMT4 (C++ for MetaTrader 4) in minutes.

docs.title: 🎯 What is CppMT4?
docs.text: CppMT4 is a type-safe C++17 client library for driving MetaTrader 4 terminals over high-performance gRPC. No DLL wrappers, no MQL4 bridge — you call a terminal in the cloud directly from C++.

docs.title: 🌟 Key advantages
docs.text:
• 🚀 High throughput — native gRPC streaming for live ticks and trade events.
  • 🛡️ Three-layer architecture — raw gRPC (MT4Account), a friendly facade (MT4Service), and one-liners (MT4Sugar).
  • 🔄 Resilient connection — automatic retry with back-off and transparent terminal re-attach.
  • 🧩 Orders, not positions — MT4's order model (market + pending in one list) surfaced natively; a rejected trade throws ApiError with the MQL4 error code.

docs.title: 📦 What to download
docs.text:
Two options, depending on what you're building:

You want… Download Why A C++ app with this SDK the whole project — git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/CppMT4.git you get the three layers, examples, demos and CMake build A client in another language / your own codegen just one file — proto/mt4_term_api.desc it's the complete, version-independent gRPC contract; run your own protoc on it in any language 
git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/CppMT4.git

CppMT4 is not on a package registry. It builds with CMake, and the protobuf/gRPC stubs are generated at build time by running your protoc on proto/mt4_term_api.desc — so they always match your installed protobuf, and the repo ships no pre-generated code. See Your First Project for the toolchain and a full build.

docs.title: 🔑 API key & authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to the MetaRPC endpoint (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) uses one of:

  1. An API key — create an account at mrpc.pro/signup, then generate a key under API Keys in the portal. Pass it to the constructor (or set MRPC_API_KEY).
  2. TRIAL access — leave the API key empty to use the shared trial gateway (fine for demo accounts and evaluation).
// explicit key:
metarpc::MT4Account account("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443, "mrpc_live_...");
// or TRIAL (empty key → MRPC_API_KEY env → "TRIAL"):
metarpc::MT4Account account("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);

docs.title: 🆔 Automatic session ID
docs.text:
MetaRPC manages the session for you:

  1. APIKey — your token (or TRIAL), sent as request metadata.
  2. id — a terminal session GUID the gateway returns from Connect / ConnectEx.

💡 You do not call GetId or supply an id before connecting. connect() performs ConnectEx, the gateway returns a session GUID, and the SDK attaches it (alongside your APIKey) to every later request and subscription automatically.

docs.title: 🔌 Minimal connection example
docs.text:
The quickest path is the high-level MT4Sugar layer:

#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);          // TRIAL access (empty key)
    sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

    std::printf("Balance: %.2f  Equity: %.2f\n", sugar.getBalance(), sugar.getEquity());
    return 0;
}

Prefer explicit control? The same thing on the low-level layer:

#include <metarpc/mt4_account.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt4_term_api;

MT4Account account("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
account.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");   // login, password, broker server name

pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance: %.2f %s\n", s.account_balance(), s.account_currency().c_str());

Note: protobuf scalar fields are accessors — s.account_balance(), not s.account_balance.

docs.title: 🗺️ Documentation road map
docs.text:
To get the most out of CppMT4, follow this reading order:

  1. 🚀 Your First Project — build and run a working project in ~10 minutes.
  2. 🗺️ Project Map — the 3 architectural layers and how they fit together.
  3. 📖 Glossary — essential MetaTrader 4 and algo-trading terms.
  4. 🐣 MT4 for Beginners — terminal setup and the demo-account walkthrough.
  5. 📡 gRPC Streaming — subscribe to ticks, trade events, order-profit and ticket snapshots, and connection state.
  6. 📊 Return Codes — MQL4 trade errors and gateway/transport error handling.

docs.title: 🏗️ Which layer should I use?
docs.text:
You want… Use Example The fastest one-liners MT4Sugar sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.1) Named struct fields, UTC times MT4Service svc.accountSummary().equity Full control / a raw field MT4Account account.accountSummary().account_balance()

🆚 Coming from MT5? MT4 has no "positions" (only orders — market + pending in one list), no DOM, and trades carry no retcode — a rejection throws ApiError with the MQL4 code. See MT4 for Beginners.

docs.title: 📖 CppMT4 Glossary
docs.text: The terms and concepts used across the CppMT4 SDK and MetaTrader 4 trading — the three layers in depth, then the C++, protocol, and trading vocabulary.

docs.title: MT4Account
docs.text:
🔹 Layer 1 — Low-level API

The base layer: direct access to the MT4 terminal over gRPC.

Key characteristics

  • Builds each protobuf *Request and attaches apikey + session id metadata.
  • Unwraps every reply's oneof { data, error } into the typed *Data payload, or throws ApiError.
  • Returns the protobuf *Data payloads — full control, maximum detail.
  • Owns the channel, stubs, retry/reconnect, and streaming (onSymbolTick, onTrade, …).
  • ~26 methods across 5 groups, plus connection/identity helpers.

When to use: you need a field or variant the higher layers don't surface, or raw protobuf control.

Location: include/metarpc/mt4_account.hpp + src/mt4_account.cpp

Docs: MT4Account Master Overview

docs.title: MT4Service
docs.text:
🔸 Layer 2 — Friendly facade

The middle layer: friendly C++ structs and plain arguments, times in UTC — no protobuf.

Key characteristics

  • Takes plain args (std::string symbols, tickets, typed enums); builds the requests for you.
  • Unwraps *Data into clean values and named structs (AccountInfo, Quote, Order, SymbolInfo, OrderResult, …).
  • Converts broker-server time ↔ UTC automatically (utcTimes = true by default).
  • The header is protobuf-free (forward-declares MT4Account) → fast compiles.
  • The same operations as MT4Account with friendly signatures; reach the layer below with account().

When to use: most application code — ergonomic, typed calls without protobuf ceremony.

Location: include/metarpc/mt4_service.hpp + src/mt4_service.cpp

Docs: MT4Service Overview

docs.title: MT4Sugar
docs.text:
🔺 Layer 3 — Convenience API

The high-level layer: business logic and one-liners.

Key characteristics

  • Order construction from side/volume; pip-based SL/TP; risk-based position sizing.
  • Compact result structs (PriceInfo, DailyStats) on top of the Service structs.
  • Order methods return the resulting ticket (0 on rejection); management methods return bool / counts — never throws on an ordinary broker rejection.
  • Also protobuf-free; reach down with service() and account().
  • ~62 methods across 11 groups — the best starting point for most apps.

Key examples

  • buyMarket(symbol, volume) — open an order in one line.
  • buyMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, slPips, tpPips) — open with a pip bracket.
  • calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, slPips) — size by risk.
  • getBalance() / getEquity() · closeAllOrders() — quick reads and an emergency exit.

When to use: rapid development, prototyping, simple strategies.

Location: include/metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp + src/mt4_sugar.cpp

Docs: MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: No async/await — blocking calls + threads
docs.text: Every unary method is an ordinary blocking function that returns a value or throws. There is no async runtime. Run work concurrently with std::thread / std::async. See Sync vs Streaming.

docs.title: Errors are exceptions
docs.text: Calls don't return error codes — they throw. ApiError = the gateway/terminal rejected the request (bad login, invalid stops, trade rejected…); it carries the MQL4 error code in mqlErrorCode. TransportError = the gRPC transport failed past the retry budget. Catch them at a sensible boundary. See Return Codes.

docs.title: Streams
docs.text: Subscriptions return a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream> (low level) or ServiceStream (friendly). The SDK reads the server stream on a background thread and invokes your callback per payload. Keep the handle alive; stop() ends it. Handle API: stop() / running() / count() / lastError(). See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: Friendly structs
docs.text: MT4Service / MT4Sugar return plain structs instead of protobuf: AccountInfo (login, balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, times…), Quote (symbol, bid, ask, high, low, UTC time), Tick (stream: +last/volume), SymbolInfo (digits, point, volume min/step/max, tick value…), Order / HistoryOrder (unified — MT4 has no separate "position"), OrderResult / CloseByResult, Bar, TradeStats, PriceInfo, DailyStats.

docs.title: Enums
docs.text: Protobuf enums are int under the hood. In C++ the generated values live at namespace scope — write pb::OO_OP_BUY, pb::ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO (not a prefixed form). The friendly layers add typed C++ enums (OrderType, Timeframe, TradeMode). See Enums Reference.

docs.title: ClientOptions
docs.text: Per-client transport knobs: unaryTimeoutMs, tradeTimeoutMs, connectTimeoutMs, maxRetries, maxBackoffMs, rootCertsPath, verbose. Reach them via options().

docs.title: 🔌 gRPC & protocol
docs.text:
• gRPC — the RPC protocol the SDK uses to reach the MetaRPC gateway (HTTP/2 + TLS).
  • grpc++ / protobuf — the C++ libraries the SDK links against (from your toolchain, via pkg-config).
  • proto/mt4_term_api.desc (mt4_term_api) — the gRPC contract as a version-independent FileDescriptorSet. CMake runs protoc on it at build time to generate the C++ + gRPC stubs (namespace mt4_term_api, aliased pb inside the SDK) into build/generated/, matching your installed protobuf.
  • *Request / *Data / *Reply — a call sends a *Request; the server answers a *Reply carrying a *Data payload or an Error.
  • oneof { data, error } — how most replies wrap the result; MT4Account unwraps it to *Data or throws ApiError.
  • apikey — your MetaRPC token ("" → MRPC_API_KEY env, else "TRIAL"), sent as metadata on every call.
  • session id / Terminal GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) — the terminal session the gateway assigns on connect() (ConnectEx), auto-attached to later calls; read via terminalGuid().
  • ConnectEx — the RPC that starts/attaches an MT4 terminal for your account; connect() calls it.
  • No RetCode on MT4 — unlike MT5's 10009 = DONE, MT4 trades return no success code. A rejection throws ApiError whose mqlErrorCode is the MQL4 error (132 market closed, 130 invalid stops, …). See Return Codes.

docs.title: 💹 Market & prices
docs.text:
Term Meaning Symbol A tradable instrument (EURUSD); names are broker-specific (suffixes like .m). Bid / Ask Best sell / best buy price. Spread = ask − bid. MT4 quotes carry no last/volume (those live on SymbolInfo / the tick stream). Point Smallest price step (point), e.g. 0.00001 for 5-digit EURUSD. Pip 10 × point on 3/5-digit symbols (EURUSD 1 pip = 0.0001). Digits Decimal places in the price (digits). Tick One price update; tick value = money per tick per lot (tickValueWithSize). Contract size Units per lot (e.g. 100,000 for FX). Volume / lot Trade size; bounded by volumeMin / volumeStep / volumeMax. Bar One OHLC candle for a Timeframe (M1…MN1); timeframes are minute counts (H1 = 60). Market Watch The terminal's selected-symbols list; a symbol must be selected (symbolSelect) before it quotes or trades.

🆚 No DOM. MT4 has no Depth-of-Market / Level-II book (MT5 does).

docs.title: 📈 Orders (no positions on MT4)
docs.text:
In MT4 there is no separate "position" object — an open market order is the position, and market + pending orders share one list (told apart by order_type):

  • Order — an instruction to trade. Market (OO_OP_BUY / OO_OP_SELL) fills now; pending rests until price triggers it.
  • Pending order — Limit (buy below / sell above the market) and Stop (buy above / sell below). No stop-limit on MT4.
  • Order type — 0 Buy, 1 Sell, 2 BuyLimit, 3 SellLimit, 4 BuyStop, 5 SellStop (MQL4 OP_*), plus 6 Balance / 7 Credit in history. Three enums share these values: OO_OP_* (reading), OC_OP_* (sending), SUB_OP_* (streams).
  • SL / TP — protective Stop-Loss / Take-Profit exit prices.
  • Stops level (TradeStopsLevel) — minimum distance SL/TP may sit from the market, in points (violate it → MQL4 130).
  • Freeze level — distance within which modify/close is blocked.
  • Slippage / deviation — allowed price movement between request and fill, in points.
  • Magic number — a client id tagging orders from one strategy. Filter with openedOrders(magic).
  • Ticket — the numeric id of an order (int32 on MT4).
  • Close-by — netting one order against an opposite order on the same symbol (orderCloseBy), saving a spread.

docs.title: 💰 Account & money
docs.text:
Term Meaning Balance Realized funds, excluding floating P/L. Equity Balance + floating P/L (live account value). Margin Funds reserved to hold open orders. Free margin equity − margin; available for new orders. Margin level equity / margin × 100, in percent (0 when flat). Leverage Borrowing ratio (e.g. 1:100). Floating / unrealized P/L Profit of still-open orders (equity − balance — MT4 has no dedicated profit field). Realized P/L Profit of closed orders (from ordersHistory).

Unlike MT5, MT4's AccountSummaryData carries margin / free-margin / margin-level directly — there is no separate margin call.

docs.title: 🕐 Time
docs.text:
• Broker server time — the raw time on the wire; MT4Account returns it unchanged (every message also carries a _utc field).
  • UTC conversion — MT4Service / MT4Sugar convert to/from UTC using the broker offset (serverOffsetSeconds / serverTimezone). With utcTimes = true (the default) every time you see and pass is UTC.

docs.title: 🛡️ Strategy mechanics
docs.text:
• Breakeven — moving SL to (around) the entry once in profit, to remove risk.
  • Trailing stop — an SL that follows price in the favorable direction, ratcheting and never loosening.
  • Risk sizing — choosing lot size so a stop-out risks a fixed % of balance (calculatePositionSize).
  • Orchestrator — a small strategy manager (loop: read → act → repeat) built on MT4Sugar: Trailing Stop, Grid Trader, Risk Manager.
  • Preset — a coordinator that classifies the market and dispatches to an orchestrator: Adaptive Market Mode. See Strategies.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• Getting Started · Project Map · MT4 for Beginners
  • Return Codes · Enums Reference · gRPC Streaming · Protobuf Inspector

docs.title: gRPC Streaming & Subscription Management
docs.text: How to subscribe to live data in CppMT4, consume it cleanly, and shut it down — the callback-on-a-background-thread way.

docs.title: The model in one line
docs.text:
A streaming call returns a std::unique_ptr<…Stream> and invokes your callback on a background reader thread for each payload. To unsubscribe, let the handle go out of scope or call stop() — the reader thread is joined for you. Keep the handle alive to keep receiving.

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req;
req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
auto stream = account.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (d.has_symbol_tick())
        std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n", d.symbol_tick().symbol().c_str(),
                    d.symbol_tick().bid(), d.symbol_tick().ask());
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
stream->stop();   // or just let `stream` go out of scope → unsubscribed

The handle exposes stop(), running(), count(), lastError().

⚠️ The callback runs on another thread — synchronize shared state (mutex/atomic) and keep it short.

docs.title: The five streams
docs.text:
On MT4Account (raw protobuf payloads → AccountStream):

Method Pushes onSymbolTick(req, cb) live ticks for the given symbols (bid/ask + last + volume) onTrade(req, cb) order/trade events (new / updated / removed / new-history) onOpenedOrdersTickets(req, cb) the open-order ticket lists on a timer (market + pending) onOpenedOrdersProfit(req, cb) per-order floating P/L + account snapshot on a timer onConnectState(req, cb) terminal connection-state events

On MT4Service the same five deliver friendly structs (times in UTC) → ServiceStream: subscribeTicks, streamTradeUpdates, streamOpenedTickets, streamOrderProfits, streamConnectState.

docs.title: A) Raw (MT4Account, full control)
docs.text:
You read protobuf payloads and guard sub-fields with has_*:

namespace pb = mt4_term_api;

pb::OnSymbolTickRequest req; req.add_symbol_names("EURUSD");
auto s = account.onSymbolTick(req, [](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (!d.has_symbol_tick()) return;
    const auto& t = d.symbol_tick();
    // raw accessors, last + volume available on the tick stream
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f last %.5f\n", t.symbol().c_str(), t.bid(), t.ask(), t.last());
});

docs.title: B) Friendly (MT4Service, simplest)
docs.text:
The friendly layer converts each payload to a struct and hands it to your callback:

auto s = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD", "GBPUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) {
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n", t.symbol.c_str(), t.bid, t.ask);
});

Also: service.streamOrderProfits(cb, 1000) → OrderProfitEvent, service.streamOpenedTickets(cb, 1000) → TicketsSnapshot.

docs.title: Bounded consumption
docs.text: Streams run until the handle dies. Common ways to bound them:

docs.title: Stop after N payloads
docs.text:
std::atomic<int> n{0};
AccountStream* raw = nullptr;
auto s = account.onSymbolTick(req, [&](const pb::OnSymbolTickData& d) {
    if (d.has_symbol_tick() && ++n >= 10 && raw) raw->stop();
});
raw = s.get();
while (s->running()) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));

docs.title: Stop after a timeout
docs.text:
auto s = account.onSymbolTick(req, cb);
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(10));
s->stop();   // unsubscribed

docs.title: Stop on a condition
docs.text:
std::atomic<bool> hit{false};
auto s = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, [&](const Tick& t) {
    if (t.bid >= 1.0950) hit = true;
});
while (!hit) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
s->stop();

For "wait until price X", MT4Sugar::waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs) already does the blocking wait for you.

docs.title: Filtering by enum
docs.text:
Stream frames carry the same enums as the rest of the API (see ENUMs Reference). Example — react only to closes on onTrade:

auto s = account.onTrade(pb::OnTradeRequest{}, [](const pb::OnTradeData& d) {
    if (!d.has_event_data()) return;
    for (const auto& o : d.event_data().removed_orders())      // order closed/deleted
        std::printf("CLOSE #%d %s P/L %+.2f\n", o.ticket(), o.symbol().c_str(), o.order_profit());
});

OnTradeData::type() / OnOpenedOrdersProfitData::type() are MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE; order rows carry SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (SUB_OP_BUY … SUB_OP_SELLSTOP). OnTradeOrderInfo::commission() is the correctly-spelled one (two m's).

docs.title: Multiple concurrent streams
docs.text:
Each stream has its own reader thread — just hold several handles at once:

auto ticks   = service.subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) { /* … */ });
auto profits = service.streamOrderProfits([](const OrderProfitEvent& e) {
    double total = 0; for (const auto& o : e.orders) total += o.profit;
    std::printf("\rfloating %.2f", total); std::fflush(stdout);
}, 1000);

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(30));
ticks->stop();
profits->stop();   // (or let both go out of scope)

Share a std::atomic / mutex-guarded structure between callbacks if they feed the same state.

docs.title: Reconnection
docs.text:
Pair streams with onConnectState (or streamConnectState) to know when the broker link drops, and re-subscribe after a reconnect:

std::atomic<bool> linkUp{true};
auto cs = service.streamConnectState([&](const ConnectState& st) {
    linkUp = st.isConnected && st.isAlive && st.apiIsAlive;
    if (!linkUp) std::puts("link down — pause trading, re-open data streams after reconnect");
});

Unary calls auto-retry transient transport errors and terminal-not-found; streams are long-lived, so re-opening them after a drop is your logic.

docs.title: ✅ Do / ❌ Don't
docs.text:
✅ Do - Keep the handle alive while you need events; stop() (or scope exit) to unsubscribe — it's deterministic. - Bound streams (count/condition + stop(), or sleep + stop()). - Synchronize callback state (mutex/atomic) and keep the callback fast. - Prefer one stream with many symbols over many single-symbol streams. - Use the friendly MT4Service streams unless you need raw protobuf fields.

❌ Don't - Don't let the handle go out of scope while you still want events — that cancels the stream. - Don't do heavy work inside the callback (it blocks the reader thread) — hand off to a queue. - Don't poll quote in a tight loop when a tick stream exists. - Don't assume "no payloads" means "broken" — a quiet market simply sends nothing (check running() / lastError()).

See also: MT4Account · Streaming Methods · MT4Service · Streaming · Sync vs Streaming

docs.title: MT4 for Beginners: Your First Steps
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is for complete beginners who have never used MetaTrader 4. We'll set up the terminal and a free demo account, then point CppMT4 at it.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 4 (MT4)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 4 is a widely-used trading platform. It lets you:

  • Trade forex, metals, commodities and more
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Run automated strategies
  • Monitor orders in real time

Think of MT4 as the "cockpit" for the markets. CppMT4 lets you control that cockpit programmatically from C++, over gRPC.

docs.title: Demo vs Live: start safely
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money. We strongly recommend it while you learn:

  • ✅ Zero risk — virtual funds (typically $10,000–$100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions — live prices and behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code — perfect for developing CppMT4 bots

A live account uses real money. Only move to live when you understand MT4, have tested your strategy thoroughly on demo, and accept the risks.

docs.title: Quick start: creating a demo account
Step 1️⃣ — Download and install the MT4 terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit the official MetaQuotes site: metatrader4.com/en/download
  2. Download the build for your OS, install and launch it.

docs.title: Step 2️⃣ — Find the Navigator panel
docs.text: On first launch MT4 usually shows a popup to open a new account. If it doesn't, find the Navigator panel (left side, below Market Watch).

docs.title: Step 3️⃣ — Open a new demo account
docs.text: In Navigator, right-click "Accounts" → "Open an account".

docs.title: Step 4️⃣ — Select a demo server
docs.text: For your first account use the simplest option — search for "MetaQuotes-Demo" / "MetaQuotes Ltd", select it, Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣ — Choose "Open a new demo account"
Step 6️⃣ — Fill in your details
docs.text: Name / email, a virtual deposit (e.g. $10,000), leverage (1:100 is a good start), currency. Accept the terms and click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣ — Save your credentials
docs.text:
MT4 shows your new account:

  • Login — account number (e.g. 591129415)
  • Password — master (trading) password
  • Investor Password — read-only
  • Server — e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo"

⚠️ Save these now. You'll need Login, Password and Server for CppMT4.

docs.title: Step 8️⃣ — Give CppMT4 your credentials
docs.text:
CppMT4's demos read credentials from environment variables (recommended — nothing to commit):

export MT4_LOGIN=591129415
export MT4_PASSWORD="YourPasswordHere"
export MT4_SERVER="MetaQuotes-Demo"
export MT4_SYMBOL="EURUSD"          # optional, default test symbol
# export MRPC_API_KEY=...           # optional; empty → TRIAL access
Variable Meaning MT4_LOGIN Your login number MT4_PASSWORD Your master password MT4_SERVER Exact broker server name from MT4 (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo) MT4_SYMBOL Default symbol the demos trade MRPC_API_KEY Your MetaRPC key, or leave empty for TRIAL access

Or in code, pass them straight to the constructor + connect: 

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(591129415, "YourPasswordHere", "MetaQuotes-Demo");

The gRPC endpoint (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) is built into the SDK — you don't set a host/port in config.

docs.title: Step 9️⃣ — Verify the MT4 connection
docs.text: In the terminal, MT4 logs into the new demo account automatically; the bottom-right corner should show a green connection indicator and your balance.

docs.title: Step 🔟 — Build and run CppMT4
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/CppMT4.git
cd CppMT4

# build the quick-start (connect → read balance → tiny trade → close)
cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build --target quickstart
./build/quickstart

# or the interactive menu of 14 demos (reads the MT4_* env vars)
cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_DEMOS=ON
cmake --build build --target demos
./build/demos

Trades CppMT4 sends appear in your MT4 terminal in real time, and the demo balance moves accordingly. Experiment freely — it's virtual money.

On Windows, CppMT4 builds with MSYS2 UCRT64 (protobuf 6.x) — see the repo README for toolchain setup.

docs.title: 🧩 MT4 password types
docs.text:
• Master password — full access (open/close trades, change settings). This is the one CppMT4 uses.
  • Investor password — view-only (see trades/balance/history, cannot trade). Good for monitoring tools. Set it in Tools → Options → Server → Change.

If you connect with the investor password, AccountInfo::investor is true and trading calls are rejected by the broker.

docs.title: Choosing a broker (optional)
docs.text:
The MetaQuotes demo is fine for practice. Later you might pick a broker for live trading or better spreads. Not financial advice — do your own research. What to look for:

  • ✅ Regulation (FCA, ASIC, CySEC, …)
  • ✅ MT4 support (specifically MT4, not only MT5)
  • ✅ Free demo (demos often expire after ~30 days of inactivity)
  • ✅ Good spreads and responsive support

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
1. Connect: Getting Started · Your First Project
  2. Understand the architecture — three layers, start wherever fits:
  3. MT4Account — raw gRPC, maximum control.
  4. MT4Service — friendly structs, most common path.
  5. MT4Sugar — one-liners, most beginner-friendly.

docs.title: Important reminders
docs.text:
• 🛡️ Security — never share your master password; use a password manager; keep credentials out of source control (use the MT4_* env vars).
  • 📊 Risk management — even on demo, build good habits: always use a stop loss, risk 1–2% per trade, understand sizing (MT4Sugar · Symbols & Risk).
  • 🧪 Testing — test all code on demo first; verify strategies over weeks, not days. Demo results don't guarantee live results.

🆚 Coming from MT5? MT4 has no "positions" (only orders — market + pending), no DOM, and a rejected trade throws ApiError with an MQL4 code instead of returning a retcode. See Return Codes.

Ready to code? Head to Getting Started and connect CppMT4 to your demo account. Good luck! 🚀

docs.title: 🗺️ CppMT4 Project Map
docs.text: The whole project as one annotated tree, with links. Links point to section overviews, never to individual method pages — open an overview to drill down into its methods.

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
CppMT4 is built in three decoupled layers (composition, not inheritance). Each layer owns the one below it, so a connected MT4Sugar gives you all three. Your code can enter at any level.

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT4Sugar include/metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp · src/mt4_sugar.cpp Convenience on top of Service: one-liners, pip-based SL/TP, risk-based sizing, batch close, quick reads. MT4Sugar overview 2 · MT4Service include/metarpc/mt4_service.hpp · src/mt4_service.cpp Friendly facade: plain args and named C++ structs, UTC times, protobuf-free header. What most code uses. MT4Service overview 1 · MT4Account include/metarpc/mt4_account.hpp · src/mt4_account.cpp Low-level gRPC: builds each proto *Request, attaches auth metadata, unwraps replies to *Data (or throws); connection & streaming. Everything builds on it. MT4Account overview 
Your code → MT4Sugar → MT4Service → MT4Account → gRPC → MetaRPC gateway → MT4 terminal

Mix freely: sugar.service() borrows the Service, service.account() (or sugar.account()) borrows the Account.

Compile-time note: mt4_service.hpp and mt4_sugar.hpp are protobuf-free (they forward-declare MT4Account), so including them does not pull in the generated protobuf headers. Only translation units that reach mt4_account.hpp — directly or via account() — pay that cost.

🆚 MT4, not MT5: there are no "positions" (market + pending orders in one list), no DOM, and no server-side pre-trade calculators. A rejected trade carries no retcode — it throws ApiError with the MQL4 error code.

docs.title: 🌳 Repository tree
docs.text:
• CppMT4/ — CMake project root
  • include/metarpc/ — the public headers
    • mt4_common.hpp — ApiError, TransportError, ClientOptions (protobuf-free, shared)
    • mt4_account.hpp — Layer 1 (pulls in protobuf) → MT4Account overview
    • mt4_service.hpp — Layer 2 + friendly structs (protobuf-free) → MT4Service overview
    • mt4_sugar.hpp — Layer 3 (protobuf-free) → MT4Sugar overview

docs.title: 🎯 Which layer should you use?
docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT4Sugar. Risk sizing, pip math and bulk ops out of the box; never throws on an ordinary broker rejection.
  • Custom execution → MT4Service. Friendly typed calls when you manage your own order shapes.
  • Protocol-level control → MT4Account. Raw proto structures and streams.

docs.title: 🔧 Transport behaviour (shared by every call)
docs.text:
• Retry — transient gRPC failures (UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) are retried with exponential back-off, up to ClientOptions::maxRetries.
  • Reconnect — a TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND transparently re-issues ConnectEx and retries, so a terminal restart is invisible to your code.
  • Errors — anything else becomes an ApiError (server said no — carries the MQL4 code) or TransportError (transport gave up). See Return Codes.

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector — Interactive Type Explorer
docs.text: An offline developer tool that explores the MT4 gRPC protobuf messages, fields and enums — browse, search, find which message declares a field, and list enum values, all without connecting to MT4.

docs.title: How it works in C++
docs.text:
Unlike Rust's prost (which keeps no runtime descriptors), the C++ protobuf runtime keeps a descriptor pool of every type compiled into the library. The inspector simply walks google::protobuf::DescriptorPool::generated_pool() — the global, generated descriptor set — so it always matches the exact types the SDK is built against. No .proto files, no network, no connection.

Source: examples/tools/protobuf_inspector.cpp.

docs.title: 🏁 Running it
docs.text:
It builds with the other tools (BUILD_TOOLS) and needs no credentials:

cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_TOOLS=ON
cmake --build build --target protobuf_inspector
./build/protobuf_inspector        # Windows: .\build\protobuf_inspector.exe

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║        🔍 PROTOBUF INSPECTOR — mt4_term_api          ║
║   Explore MT4 gRPC messages, fields & enums offline  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
Indexed 257 messages, 26 enums from the generated code.

>

docs.title: 🧰 Commands
docs.text:
Command Description Example list / ls List all message types list enums List all enum types enums <TypeName> Inspect a message — its fields and types AccountSummaryData search <text> / find <text> Search types by name search Order field <name> Find messages that contain a field field ticket enum <name> Show an enum's values enum OrderSendOperationType help / ? Help help exit / quit / q Exit exit

Type names and field names are case-insensitive.

docs.title: 1) Inspect a message's fields
docs.text:
> AccountSummaryData

╔═══ MESSAGE: AccountSummaryData ═══╗

📋 Fields:

  • #1   account_login                            : int64
  • #2   account_balance                          : double
  • #3   account_equity                           : double
  • #6   account_trade_mode                       : EnumAccountTradeMode
  • #9   server_time                              : Timestamp
  ...

#n is the protobuf field tag; the type is the proto type. repeated …, optional … and oneof … are shown where relevant, and message/enum fields show the referenced type name. In C++ these are accessors on the generated class — s.account_balance(), s.account_trade_mode().

docs.title: 2) A oneof reply
docs.text:
> AccountSummaryReply

╔═══ MESSAGE: AccountSummaryReply ═══╗

📋 Fields:

  •      response                                 : oneof response (tags 1, 2)

The *Reply messages wrap their payload in a response oneof of Data | Error — exactly what MT4Account unwraps (returning Data, throwing ApiError on Error).

docs.title: 3) Which messages have a ticket field?
docs.text:
> field ticket

📦 HistoryOrderInfo:
   └─ ticket : int32
📦 OpenedOrderInfo:
   └─ ticket : int32
📦 OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData:
   └─ position_tickets : repeated int32
   └─ pending_order_tickets : repeated int32

docs.title: 4) See an enum's values
docs.text:
> enum OrderSendOperationType

╔═══ ENUM: OrderSendOperationType ═══╗

  OC_OP_BUY                                         = 0
  OC_OP_SELL                                        = 1
  OC_OP_BUYLIMIT                                    = 2
  OC_OP_SELLLIMIT                                   = 3
  OC_OP_BUYSTOP                                     = 4
  OC_OP_SELLSTOP                                    = 5

In C++ the value names are the SCREAMING_CASE proto names at namespace scope — write pb::OC_OP_BUY. (See ENUMs Reference for the full set, including the three order-type enums OO_OP_* / OC_OP_* / SUB_OP_*.)

docs.title: 🧩 Why it's useful
docs.text:
• Find the exact field name before you write msg.some_field() — no guessing CamelCase vs snake_case (protobuf lowercases, so TradeTickValue → tradetickvalue()).
  • Discover which message carries a value with field <name>.
  • Confirm an enum's numbers with enum <name> without digging through headers.
  • Stays in sync — it reads the very descriptors the library was compiled with, so it can never drift from your types.

The sibling tool dump_descriptor_set (same BUILD_TOOLS target) writes the whole contract out as a FileDescriptorSet — that's how proto/mt4_term_api.desc is produced.

See also: ENUMs Reference · Project Map · Glossary

docs.title: Return Codes & Errors Reference — CppMT4
docs.text:
How failures reach you in CppMT4, and the MQL4 trade-error codes behind rejected orders.

⚠️ MT4 uses MQL4 error codes (0–150 for the trade server, 4000+ for MQL runtime) — not the MT5 ENUM_TRADE_RETCODE numbers (10004, 10018, 10019, …). If you've seen those, they belong to MT5.

docs.title: How errors surface
docs.text:
CppMT4 doesn't return a status you inspect — a failed call throws. There are two exception types (include/metarpc/mt4_common.hpp), both derived from std::runtime_error (so e.what() always works):

namespace metarpc {

class ApiError : public std::runtime_error {      // the gateway/terminal answered with an error
public:
    std::string code;              // gateway code, e.g. "TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND"
    std::string message;           // human-readable (includes MQL hints)
    int         mqlErrorCode;      // the MQL4 error number (0 if none) — see tables
    int         mqlTradeCode;      // MQL4 trade return code (0 if none)
    std::string mqlTradeDescription;
    std::string where;             // the RPC that failed, e.g. "OrderSend"
    bool        isInvalidLogin() const;   // bad credentials — never retried
};

class TransportError : public std::runtime_error {  // gRPC transport failed past the retry budget
public:
    int grpcCode;                  // grpc::StatusCode (14 = UNAVAILABLE, 4 = DEADLINE_EXCEEDED)
};

} // namespace metarpc
  • ApiError — the gateway returned its Error payload (a gateway code string plus an MQL code/description). A rejected trade is an ApiError with mqlErrorCode set. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND is handled by one automatic reconnect + retry before it ever reaches you.
  • TransportError — a transport failure (UNAVAILABLE / DEADLINE_EXCEEDED / CANCELLED) that outlived the automatic retry budget.
  • Bad login — ApiError::isInvalidLogin() is true; these are never retried (repeated bad logins get accounts locked).

No error ≠ nothing to check — only for reads. For trades, a returned *Data means it executed; a rejection throws, so wrap trade calls in try/catch (const ApiError&).

docs.title: The gateway Error payload → ApiError
docs.text: Proto field C++ (ApiError) Meaning error_code code Gateway code, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, CONNECT_EX_INVALID_LOGIN_ERROR error_message message Human-readable message mql_error_int_code mqlErrorCode The MQL4 error number (tables below) mql_error_description mqlTradeDescription MQL4 error text type — ErrorType category (folded into the message)

docs.title: MQL4 trade-server error codes
docs.text:
These are the ones you actually hit from trading calls (e.mqlErrorCode):

Code Name Meaning / fix 0 ERR_NO_ERROR Success 1 ERR_NO_RESULT No error, but nothing changed (e.g. modify to identical values) 2 ERR_COMMON_ERROR Generic error — retry / check connection 3 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_PARAMETERS Bad request fields 4 ERR_SERVER_BUSY Trade server busy — back off and retry 6 ERR_NO_CONNECTION No link to the trade server 8 ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS Throttle your calls 128 ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT Trade timed out — may still have executed; reconcile 129 ERR_INVALID_PRICE Price off/stale — re-quote 130 ERR_INVALID_STOPS SL/TP too close — respect TradeStopsLevel 131 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME Lot invalid — normalize to VolumeStep/min/max 132 ERR_MARKET_CLOSED Market closed — wait for session (try a 24/7 symbol) 133 ERR_TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled for the account/symbol 134 ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY Insufficient margin — smaller lot 135 ERR_PRICE_CHANGED Price moved — re-quote and resend 136 ERR_OFF_QUOTES No prices — symbol not live / illiquid 137 ERR_BROKER_BUSY Broker busy — retry 138 ERR_REQUOTE Requote — resend at the new price, or raise slippage 139 ERR_ORDER_LOCKED Order already being processed 140 ERR_LONG_POSITIONS_ONLY_ALLOWED Only buys allowed on this symbol 141 ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Too many requests — throttle 145 ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED Modify denied (too close to market / frozen) 146 ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY Trade context busy — serialize trade calls 147 ERR_TRADE_EXPIRATION_DENIED Expiration not allowed by broker 148 ERR_TRADE_TOO_MANY_ORDERS Order count limit reached 149 ERR_TRADE_HEDGE_PROHIBITED Hedging not allowed 150 ERR_TRADE_PROHIBITED_BY_FIFO FIFO rule violated

Codes 4000+ are MQL runtime errors from the terminal side — rare for API trading.

docs.title: Inspect the code
docs.text:
try {
    int ticket = sugar.service().orderSend(req).ticket;   // or account.orderSend(...)
    std::printf("opened #%d\n", ticket);
} catch (const ApiError& e) {
    switch (e.mqlErrorCode) {
        case 132: std::puts("market closed — try later");      break;
        case 134: std::puts("not enough money — size down");    break;
        case 130: std::puts("invalid stops — widen SL/TP");     break;
        case 138: std::puts("requote — resend / raise slippage"); break;
        default:  std::printf("rejected: %s (MQL4 %d)\n", e.what(), e.mqlErrorCode);
    }
} catch (const TransportError& e) {
    std::printf("transport error (code %d) — may be retryable: %s\n", e.grpcCode, e.what());
}

Sugar swallows ordinary rejections. MT4Sugar::buyMarket / closeOrder / modifyOrder* catch ApiError and return 0 / false instead of throwing — so a one-liner never throws for a normal broker refusal. Drop to MT4Service / MT4Account (as above) when you need the MQL4 code itself.

docs.title: What's retried for you
docs.text:
The internal call<> wrapper auto-retries transient gRPC (UNAVAILABLE / DEADLINE_EXCEEDED / CANCELLED) and performs one reconnect on TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND. Trade calls are not retried blindly — a timed-out orderSend may have filled, so on error reconcile with openedOrders before resending.

See also: ENUMs Reference · OrderSend · MT4Sugar · Trading

docs.title: Synchronous Calls vs Streaming — How CppMT4 Executes
docs.text: CppMT4's execution model in one line: unary calls block; streams run on a background thread and call you back. There is no async/await and no CompletionQueue to manage — the SDK hides the gRPC machinery.

docs.title: 🎯 Two execution modes
docs.text: Unary (request → reply) Streaming (subscription) Style synchronous, blocks until the reply callback on a background thread Examples accountSummary, quote, orderSend, ordersHistory onSymbolTick, onTrade, onOpenedOrdersProfit, … Returns the value (or throws ApiError / TransportError) a stream handle; delivers payloads until stopped You manage nothing — call it and read the result keep the handle alive; stop() to cancel Good for account reads, placing/closing orders, history live ticks, trade events, health monitoring

docs.title: 🔁 Unary calls — synchronous and blocking
docs.text:
Every non-streaming method is a blocking round-trip. Transient failures are retried with back-off and a dropped terminal is re-attached automatically, so you don't poll or retry yourself.

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");   // blocks until ready

double balance = sugar.getBalance();                     // blocks, returns the value
int ticket     = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);        // blocks, returns the ticket (0 = rejected)

Deadlines come from ClientOptions (unaryTimeoutMs for reads, tradeTimeoutMs for trades). Tune them via account().options() / service().options().

docs.title: 📡 Streaming — background thread + callbacks
docs.text:
Each onX() / stream* opens a server stream and invokes your callback on a dedicated background thread. Keep the returned handle alive to keep receiving; destroy it or call stop() to cancel.

auto stream = sugar.service().subscribeTicks({"EURUSD"}, [](const Tick& t) {
    // ⚠️ runs on another thread — synchronize shared state, keep this short
    std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f\n", t.symbol.c_str(), t.bid, t.ask);
});

std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
stream->stop();   // (also happens automatically when `stream` is destroyed)

The handle exposes stop(), running(), count() and lastError() — see gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: 💡 Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Reads and trades → call the unary method directly; it blocks and returns (or throws).
  • Live data / monitoring → subscribe to a stream; handle events in the callback.
  • Don't poll a quote in a tight loop when a tick stream will push it to you.
  • Guard callback state with a mutex/atomic — callbacks fire on a background thread.
  • One thread, many streams is fine; the SDK runs each stream's reader independently.

🆚 Coming from an async SDK (Rust/Python)? CppMT4 is not async/await-based. Unary calls simply block; concurrency comes from running your own threads and from the background reader threads behind streams.

docs.title: Writing Your Own Code (Scratchpad)
docs.text:
How to spin up your own CppMT4 program with the connection boilerplate already handled — the fastest way to try an idea against a live demo terminal.

Unlike the Python SDK's 18_usercode.py slot, CppMT4 is a compiled library, so "your sandbox" is simply your own .cpp that links the SDK. There are two easy starting points.

docs.title: Option A — start from quickstart.cpp
docs.text:
The repo ships examples/quickstart.cpp: connect → read balance → tiny trade → close. Copy it and edit the middle:

#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);          // empty key → TRIAL access
    sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");   // your demo creds

    // ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    //  YOUR CODE HERE
    // ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    std::printf("Balance: %.2f\n", sugar.getBalance());
    std::printf("EURUSD %.5f / %.5f\n", sugar.getBid("EURUSD"), sugar.getAsk("EURUSD"));

    // e.g. open and close a tiny demo order:
    // int t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
    // if (t) sugar.closeOrder(t);
    // ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    return 0;
}

Build & run:

cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build --target quickstart
./build/quickstart

docs.title: Option B — the ready sandbox demo (ships in the repo)
docs.text:
A ready-to-edit scratchpad already ships at examples/demos/sandbox/99_sandbox.cpp, wired into the demos menu as [18]. It reuses the demos' connection + config helpers, so you never hard-code credentials — sugar arrives already connected. Just edit the marked block:

void demo_sandbox(MT4Sugar& sugar, const Config& cfg) {
    printSub("Sandbox — write your own code");

    // ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    //  YOUR CODE HERE — sugar is already connected
    std::cout << "balance " << sugar.getBalance() << "\n";
    for (const auto& o : sugar.getOpenOrders())
        std::cout << "  #" << o.ticket << " " << o.symbol << " P/L " << o.profit << "\n";

    //  ⚠ uncomment to trade:
    //  int t = sugar.buyMarket(cfg.testSymbol, cfg.testVolume);
    //  if (t) sugar.closeOrder(t);
    // ────────────────────────────────────────────────
}

Credentials come from the environment, so nothing secret goes in the file:

export MT4_LOGIN=... MT4_PASSWORD=... MT4_SERVER="EGlobal-Demo"
cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_DEMOS=ON
cmake --build build --target demos
./build/demos 18        # runs your sandbox directly, or pick [18] from the menu

It's already registered in examples/demos/demos.hpp + main.cpp (menu entry [18]); the CMake glob (examples/demos/*.cpp, recursive) compiles it automatically. Add more sandbox files beside it the same way.

docs.title: What's already handled for you
docs.text:
Concern Taken care of by Connection sugar.connect(...) (or the demos' helpers/connection.hpp) performs ConnectEx and blocks until ready Session id / API key attached to every request automatically — you never call GetId Reconnect / retry the SDK retries transient errors and re-attaches a dropped terminal Credentials MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER (+ MRPC_API_KEY) env vars via config/config.hpp

You reach down a layer any time: sugar.service() for the friendly facade, sugar.account() for raw protobuf RPCs.

docs.title: Handy one-liners to try
docs.text:
sugar.getBalance();  sugar.getEquity();  sugar.getProfit();          // account money
sugar.getBid("EURUSD");  sugar.getSpread("EURUSD");                  // prices
sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", 0.01, /*SL*/ 20, /*TP*/ 40);      // trade with pips
sugar.getOpenOrders();  sugar.getTotalProfit();  sugar.closeAllOrders();
sugar.getHistoryToday();  sugar.getDailyStats();                     // history / stats
sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", /*risk%*/ 1.0, /*SL pips*/ 20); // risk sizing

Full menus: MT4Sugar · MT4Service · MT4Account.

⚠️ Trading one-liners run live on the connected account. Keep volumes tiny on demo, and remember buyMarket returns 0 (never throws) when the broker rejects — check the return.

See also: Your First Project · Getting Started · MT4Sugar Overview

docs.title: Your First Project in 10 Minutes (C++)
docs.text: Hands-on quick start — build a working MetaTrader 4 bot with CppMT4 from scratch.

docs.title: Step 0 — API key (or TRIAL)
docs.text:
To reach the MetaRPC endpoint (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) you need either an API key or TRIAL access:

  1. Register at mrpc.pro/signup and copy a key from mrpc.pro/my, or
  2. leave the key empty to use TRIAL access (fine for demo accounts).

You'll also need demo account credentials — login, password, and the broker server name (e.g. EGlobal-Demo).

docs.title: Step 1 — get the SDK
docs.text:
Building a C++ app? Clone the whole project:

git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/CppMT4.git
cd CppMT4

The SDK is header + source under include/metarpc/ and src/; the gRPC stubs are generated at build time from proto/mt4_term_api.desc.

Building in another language (or your own codegen) instead? You don't need the whole repo — just grab the single contract file proto/mt4_term_api.desc and run your own protoc on it. See What to download.

docs.title: Step 2 — write your bot
docs.text:
The fastest path is the high-level MT4Sugar layer. Create main.cpp:

#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    // TRIAL access (empty API key). Pass your key as the 3rd arg if you have one.
    MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);

    // login, password, broker server name
    sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");
    std::printf("Connected. Balance %.2f  Equity %.2f\n",
                sugar.getBalance(), sugar.getEquity());

    // current price
    std::printf("EURUSD %.5f / %.5f\n", sugar.getBid("EURUSD"), sugar.getAsk("EURUSD"));

    // ⚠️ open a tiny demo BUY, then close it (returns 0 if the broker rejects it)
    int ticket = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.01);
    if (ticket) {
        std::printf("opened #%d\n", ticket);
        sugar.closeOrder(ticket);
        std::puts("closed");
    } else {
        std::puts("order rejected (market closed? try a 24/7 symbol like BTCUSD)");
    }
    return 0;
}

🆚 MT4: buyMarket returns an int ticket — 0 means the broker rejected it (it never throws for an ordinary rejection). There are no "positions": you close the order with closeOrder(ticket).

docs.title: Step 3 — build & run
docs.text:
CppMT4 builds with CMake (MSYS2 UCRT64 / protobuf 6.x on Windows). The repo ships a ready examples/quickstart.cpp that does exactly the above:

cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build --target quickstart
./build/quickstart        # Windows: .\build\quickstart.exe

Pass your credentials via environment variables and run the full demo menu instead:

# MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER (+ optional MT4_SYMBOL / MT4_VOLUME)
cmake -B build -S . -DBUILD_DEMOS=ON
cmake --build build --target demos
./build/demos            # interactive menu of 14 demos

docs.title: 🆚 MT4 vs MT5 — what's different here
docs.text:
MT4 is order-centric, not position-centric. If you know the MT5 SDK, keep these in mind:

  • No "positions". There are only orders. openedOrders() returns live market orders and pending orders in one list (order_infos). There is no positionsTotal / PositionInfo split.
  • Tickets are int32, not int64.
  • 6 order types (OO_OP_BUY … OO_OP_SELLSTOP) — no stop-limit. History may also carry Balance/Credit pseudo-orders.
  • No Depth-of-Market (DOM) and no orderCalcMargin / orderCalcProfit / orderCheck — MT4 has no server-side pre-trade calculators. Use tickValueWithSize + symbolParamsMany and compute client-side (the MT4Service / MT4Sugar layers do this for you).
  • Quotes, not ticks. quote / quoteMany return bid/ask plus session high/low (no last/volume).
  • Trading has no retcode. A rejected trade throws ApiError carrying the MQL4 error code (e.g. 130 invalid stops, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money) — there is no 10009-style status field on OrderSendData.
  • Timeframes are in MINUTES (M1=1, H1=60, D1=1440) on the wire.
  • Every message carries both server time and a _utc field (e.g. open_time / open_time_utc); the raw layer gives you both, the MT4Service layer picks one for you.

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
Every method is called on an MT4Account (#include <metarpc/mt4_account.hpp>, namespace metarpc). It owns the gRPC channel, sends the terminal id and API key as metadata, retries transient failures, re-attaches a dropped terminal session, and unwraps the reply — returning the protobuf *Data payload or throwing.

#include <metarpc/mt4_account.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;
namespace pb = mt4_term_api;              // the generated protobuf namespace

// Create the account (prepares the gRPC channel)
MT4Account account("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);

// Connect the terminal (login, password, broker server name)
account.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");
// The gateway returns a terminal session GUID; later calls reuse it automatically.

// Call a method: returns the Data payload, or throws ApiError / TransportError
pb::AccountSummaryData s = account.accountSummary();
std::printf("Balance: $%.2f\n", s.account_balance());

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • C++ call: account.method(const pb::Request&) returns pb::MethodData (by value)
  • Reply structure: the gRPC reply carries either a Data payload or an Error; MT4Account returns the Data and turns Error into a thrown ApiError (server-side error) — transport failures past the retry budget throw TransportError
  • Trading errors: a rejected trade throws ApiError with the MQL4 error code in mqlErrorCode (e.g. 132 market closed) — there is no success return code.

Timestamps: proto uses google.protobuf.Timestamp (or raw int64 unix seconds on some messages). The raw layer gives you broker/server time and a _utc field; the friendly MT4Service layer selects UTC for you.

Streaming methods: return a std::unique_ptr<AccountStream>. The SDK reads the stream on a background thread and invokes your callback for each message; keep the handle alive and call stop() to end it.
