docs.text:
MT4Account (low) MT4Service (mid) Arguments build *Request protobuf plain values Returns protobuf *Data (getters) friendly structs / std::vector Times broker + _utc fields one int64_t, UTC by default Header pulls in protobuf protobuf-free (fast compile) Enums pb::OO_OP_* / pb::OC_OP_* OrderType, Timeframe, TradeMode

Up next: MT4Sugar — one-liners on top of this facade.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 1. Connection & Account
docs.text:
Connect, check liveness, and read account money figures — each a self-contained one-liner. The balance/margin getters each fetch one fresh account summary.

#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;
MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
void connect(int64_t login, const std::string& password, const std::string& server,
             const std::string& name = "", int timeoutSeconds = 120);
void quickConnect();   // reads MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER from the environment
bool isConnected() const;
bool ping();           // lightweight liveness: fetches the account summary, true on success
void disconnect();     // drop the channel (the terminal keeps running)
  • connect(...) — same arguments as the lower layers; blocks until the terminal is ready.
  • quickConnect() — one-liner for demos/CI; throws std::runtime_error if any MT4_* env var is missing.
  • ping() — a cheap "is the link alive?" check.
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");
// or, from env vars:
// sugar.quickConnect();

if (sugar.ping()) std::puts("alive");

docs.title: Balance & margin
docs.text:
double getBalance();        // account balance (no floating P/L)
double getEquity();         // balance + floating P/L
double getMargin();         // used margin
double getFreeMargin();     // free margin
double getMarginLevel();    // margin level, %
double getProfit();         // current floating profit (equity - balance)

Each reads a fresh account summary. For several figures at once, prefer getAccountInfo() (one call) over calling these back-to-back.

std::printf("bal %.2f  eq %.2f  free %.2f  float %.2f\n",
            sugar.getBalance(), sugar.getEquity(), sugar.getFreeMargin(), sugar.getProfit());

if (sugar.getMarginLevel() > 0 && sugar.getMarginLevel() < 150)
    std::puts("⚠️ margin level low");

docs.title: getAccountInfo()
docs.text:
AccountInfo getAccountInfo();

The full account snapshot in one call — login, currency, balance, equity, margin, marginFree, marginLevel, leverage, tradeMode, … (same AccountInfo struct as MT4Service · Account.)

AccountInfo a = sugar.getAccountInfo();
std::printf("%lld  %.2f %s  lev 1:%lld  %s\n",
            (long long)a.login, a.equity, a.currency.c_str(), (long long)a.leverage,
            a.tradeAllowed ? "trading on" : "trading off");

Tip: getBalance() / getEquity() / … are convenience wrappers; when you need many fields, one getAccountInfo() is cheaper than several getters.

docs.title: Connect from the environment, fail cleanly
docs.text:
#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
#include <cstdio>
using namespace metarpc;

int main() {
    MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
    try {
        sugar.quickConnect();                       // reads MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::printf("connect failed: %s\n", e.what());
        return 1;
    }
    std::printf("connected as %lld\n", (long long)sugar.getAccountInfo().login);
}

docs.title: One-call account dashboard
docs.text:
void dashboard(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    AccountInfo a = sugar.getAccountInfo();          // one round-trip, not six getters
    double floating = a.equity - a.balance;          // MT4 has no profit field
    std::printf("Acc %lld | %s | Bal %.2f | Eq %.2f | Float %+.2f | Free %.2f | Lvl %.0f%%\n",
                (long long)a.login, a.currency.c_str(), a.balance, a.equity,
                floating, a.marginFree, a.marginLevel);
}

docs.title: Health-gated loop with auto-reconnect check
docs.text:
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>
void runWhileHealthy(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    while (true) {
        if (!sugar.ping()) {                         // cheap liveness probe
            std::puts("link down — backing off");
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
            continue;
        }
        // ... your per-tick logic using sugar ...
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(1));
    }
}

docs.title: Pre-trade affordability guard
docs.text:
bool canAfford(MT4Sugar& sugar, double neededMargin) {
    return sugar.getFreeMargin() > neededMargin * 1.5;   // keep 50% headroom
}

Back to: MT4Sugar — Overview · Next: 2. Prices

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 2. Prices
docs.text:
Current prices and spread in one line, plus a blocking wait-for-price helper. All read live quotes under the hood.

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

docs.title: getBid / getAsk / getSpread
docs.text:
double getBid(const std::string& symbol);      // current bid
double getAsk(const std::string& symbol);      // current ask
double getSpread(const std::string& symbol);   // ask - bid (price units)

std::printf("EURUSD %.5f / %.5f  spread %.5f\n",
            sugar.getBid("EURUSD"), sugar.getAsk("EURUSD"), sugar.getSpread("EURUSD"));

For several figures at once, prefer getPriceInfo() (one call) over three separate getters.

docs.title: getPriceInfo(symbol)
docs.text:
PriceInfo getPriceInfo(const std::string& symbol);

Bid, ask, spread and quote time in one call.

Returns — PriceInfo: symbol, bid, ask, spread (ask − bid), time (UTC seconds).

PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo("EURUSD");
std::printf("%s %.5f/%.5f  spread %.5f\n", p.symbol.c_str(), p.bid, p.ask, p.spread);

docs.title: waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs=10000)
docs.text:
PriceInfo waitForPrice(const std::string& symbol, double targetBid, int timeoutMs = 10000);

Poll until the bid reaches targetBid (or just any tick when targetBid == 0), up to timeoutMs. Returns the last price seen; on timeout the returned PriceInfo has an empty symbol.

PriceInfo hit = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 1.10000, /*timeoutMs*/ 5000);
if (hit.symbol.empty()) std::puts("timed out");
else std::printf("reached %.5f\n", hit.bid);

// any next tick:
PriceInfo next = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 0.0, 2000);

Blocking. waitForPrice polls on the calling thread. For push-style updates use MT4Service::subscribeTicks.

docs.title: Skip entries when the spread is too wide
docs.text:
bool spreadOK(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double maxPips) {
    PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo(sym);
    double point = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym).point;
    double pip   = (sugar.getSymbolDigits(sym) % 2 == 1) ? point * 10 : point;
    return (p.spread / pip) <= maxPips;             // e.g. don't trade if spread > 3 pips
}

docs.title: Watchlist snapshot table
docs.text:
void snapshot(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::vector<std::string>& syms) {
    std::printf("%-8s %12s %12s %10s\n", "SYMBOL", "BID", "ASK", "SPREAD");
    for (const auto& s : syms) {
        PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo(s);
        std::printf("%-8s %12.5f %12.5f %10.5f\n", s.c_str(), p.bid, p.ask, p.spread);
    }
}

docs.title: Wait for a breakout, then act
docs.text:
// block until EURUSD prints 1.1000+, up to 30s, then enter
PriceInfo hit = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 1.10000, /*timeoutMs*/ 30000);
if (!hit.symbol.empty()) {
    int t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.10);
    std::printf(t ? "entered #%d\n" : "entry rejected\n", t);
} else {
    std::puts("no breakout within 30s");
}

docs.title: Mid price & simple momentum tick
docs.text:
double mid(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym) {
    PriceInfo p = sugar.getPriceInfo(sym);
    return (p.bid + p.ask) / 2.0;
}
// sample twice to see direction
double a = mid(sugar, "EURUSD");
PriceInfo next = sugar.waitForPrice("EURUSD", 0.0, 2000);   // any next tick
double b = next.symbol.empty() ? a : (next.bid + next.ask) / 2.0;
std::printf("%s\n", b > a ? "up" : b < a ? "down" : "flat");

Back to: MT4Sugar — Overview · Next: 3. Trading

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 3. Trading
docs.text:
Open market and pending orders in one line. Every helper returns the ticket (int) — or 0 on an ordinary rejection (it never throws for a broker refusal; the MQL4 error is swallowed into the 0).

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

🛑 0 = rejected. Always check the return. (Underlying throw model: MT4Account · OrderSend.)

docs.title: Simple market & pending
docs.text:
int buyMarket (const std::string& symbol, double volume);
int sellMarket(const std::string& symbol, double volume);
int buyLimit  (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);
int sellLimit (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);
int buyStop   (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);
int sellStop  (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price);
  • Market: buyMarket / sellMarket fill at the current price.
  • Limit: sits better than market (buy below, sell above).
  • Stop: sits worse than market (buy above, sell below).
int t = sugar.buyMarket("EURUSD", 0.10);
if (!t) std::puts("rejected");

sugar.sellLimit("EURUSD", 0.10, 1.10500);   // pending sell-limit above market

docs.title: With stop-loss / take-profit (absolute prices)
docs.text:
int buyMarketWithSLTP (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double sl, double tp);
int sellMarketWithSLTP(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double sl, double tp);
int buyLimitWithSLTP  (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price, double sl, double tp);
int sellLimitWithSLTP (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double price, double sl, double tp);

sl / tp are prices (use calculateSLTP to derive them from pip distances).

int t = sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.10, /*sl*/ 1.09500, /*tp*/ 1.10500);

// pending buy-limit with stops
sugar.buyLimitWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.10, /*price*/ 1.09000, /*sl*/ 1.08500, /*tp*/ 1.10000);

docs.title: With stop-loss / take-profit (pip distances)
docs.text:
int buyMarketWithPips (const std::string& symbol, double volume, double slPips, double tpPips);
int sellMarketWithPips(const std::string& symbol, double volume, double slPips, double tpPips);

SL/TP given as pip distances from entry — the helper computes the prices for you (pip = point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols).

int t = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", 0.10, /*SL*/ 20, /*TP*/ 40);

docs.title: Size by risk, then enter with a bracket
docs.text:
double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", /*risk%*/ 1.0, /*SL pips*/ 20);
int ticket  = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, 20, 40);   // 1:2 reward:risk
if (ticket) std::printf("opened #%d, %.2f lots\n", ticket, lots);

docs.title: Safe entry — validate, then trade
docs.text:
bool safeBuy(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double lots, double slPips, double tpPips) {
    std::string why;
    if (!sugar.canOpenOrder(sym, lots, why)) { std::printf("skip: %s\n", why.c_str()); return false; }
    int t = sugar.buyMarketWithPips(sym, lots, slPips, tpPips);
    if (!t) { std::puts("broker rejected"); return false; }
    std::printf("opened #%d\n", t);
    return true;
}

docs.title: Pending-order ladder (accumulate on dips)
docs.text:
void buyLadder(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double lots, int rungs, double gapPips) {
    double point = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym).point;
    double pip   = (sugar.getSymbolDigits(sym) % 2 == 1) ? point * 10 : point;
    double bid   = sugar.getBid(sym);
    for (int i = 1; i <= rungs; ++i) {
        int t = sugar.buyLimit(sym, lots, bid - i * gapPips * pip);
        std::printf(t ? "  rung %d #%d\n" : "  rung %d rejected\n", i, t);
    }
}

docs.title: Retry a requoted market order
docs.text:
int buyRetry(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double lots, int tries = 3) {
    for (int i = 0; i < tries; ++i) {
        int t = sugar.buyMarket(sym, lots);          // 0 on rejection (requote/price changed)
        if (t) return t;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(200));   // let price settle
    }
    return 0;
}

docs.title: Market order with explicit SL/TP prices
docs.text:
double entry = sugar.getAsk("EURUSD");
double sl, tp;
sugar.calculateSLTP("EURUSD", "buy", entry, /*SLpips*/ 25, /*TPpips*/ 50, sl, tp);
int t = sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP("EURUSD", 0.10, sl, tp);

Back to: MT4Sugar — Overview · Next: 4. Order Management

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 4. Order Management & Info
docs.text:
Close, modify and inspect live orders. Remember MT4 has no "positions" — these cover market and pending orders.

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

docs.title: Closing
docs.text:
bool closeOrder(int ticket);                        // close a market order / delete a pending
bool closeOrderPartial(int ticket, double lots);    // close part of a market order
int  closeAllOrders();                              // close/delete every order; returns count
int  closeAllBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);   // same, for one symbol; returns count

closeOrder / closeOrderPartial return false on an ordinary rejection (they don't throw). The closeAll* variants return how many were closed.

sugar.closeOrder(ticket);                 // full close / delete
sugar.closeOrderPartial(ticket, 0.05);    // scale out 0.05 lots
int n = sugar.closeAllOrders();
std::printf("closed %d orders\n", n);

docs.title: Modifying
docs.text:
bool modifyOrderSL(int ticket, double sl);                  // set SL only (keeps TP)
bool modifyOrderTP(int ticket, double tp);                  // set TP only (keeps SL)
bool modifyOrderSLTP(int ticket, double sl, double tp);     // set both

sl / tp are prices. All three return false instead of throwing on an ordinary rejection (e.g. stops too close → MQL4 130).

sugar.modifyOrderSLTP(ticket, /*sl*/ 1.09000, /*tp*/ 1.11000);
sugar.modifyOrderSL(ticket, 1.09500);     // move the stop up (keep TP)

docs.title: Inspecting
docs.text:
std::vector<Order> getOpenOrders();                            // all live orders
std::vector<Order> getOrdersBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);
Order getOrderByTicket(int ticket, bool& found);               // found=false if none
bool  hasOpenOrder(const std::string& symbol);                 // any order on the symbol?
int   countOpenOrders();                                       // number of live orders
double getTotalProfit();                                       // summed floating profit
double getProfitBySymbol(const std::string& symbol);           // floating profit on one symbol

The Order struct (ticket, symbol, type, lots, prices, SL/TP, profit, …) is the same as MT4Service · Orders; use o.isPending() / o.isBuy().

std::printf("%d open, floating %.2f\n", sugar.countOpenOrders(), sugar.getTotalProfit());

bool found;
Order o = sugar.getOrderByTicket(ticket, found);
if (found) std::printf("#%d %s %.2f lots, P/L %.2f\n", o.ticket, o.symbol.c_str(), o.lots, o.profit);

if (sugar.hasOpenOrder("EURUSD"))
    std::printf("EURUSD exposure P/L %.2f\n", sugar.getProfitBySymbol("EURUSD"));

docs.title: Close every losing market order
docs.text:
int cutLosers(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    int n = 0;
    for (const auto& o : sugar.getOpenOrders())
        if (!o.isPending() && o.profit < 0 && sugar.closeOrder(o.ticket)) ++n;
    return n;
}

docs.title: Take partial profit at a target
docs.text:
void scaleOut(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double takeProfitCash) {
    if (sugar.getProfitBySymbol(sym) < takeProfitCash) return;
    for (const auto& o : sugar.getOrdersBySymbol(sym))
        if (!o.isPending() && o.profit > 0)
            sugar.closeOrderPartial(o.ticket, o.lots / 2.0);   // bank half
}

docs.title: Move every open order to break-even once in profit
docs.text:
void breakEvenAll(MT4Sugar& sugar, double triggerProfit) {
    for (const auto& o : sugar.getOpenOrders()) {
        if (o.isPending() || o.profit < triggerProfit) continue;
        sugar.modifyOrderSL(o.ticket, o.openPrice);            // SL → entry, keep TP
    }
}

docs.title: Flatten a symbol on a cash stop
docs.text:
void capLoss(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double maxLoss) {
    if (sugar.getProfitBySymbol(sym) <= -maxLoss)
        std::printf("closed %d on %s\n", sugar.closeAllBySymbol(sym), sym.c_str());
}

docs.title: Status line of live exposure
docs.text:
void status(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    std::printf("open %d | floating %.2f\n", sugar.countOpenOrders(), sugar.getTotalProfit());
}

Back to: MT4Sugar — Overview · Next: 5. History & Statistics

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 5. History & Statistics
docs.text:
Closed-order history over ready-made windows, period profits, and a one-call daily summary. Day boundaries are UTC.

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

docs.title: History windows
docs.text:
std::vector<HistoryOrder> getHistoryToday();
std::vector<HistoryOrder> getHistoryYesterday();
std::vector<HistoryOrder> getHistoryThisWeek();
std::vector<HistoryOrder> getHistoryThisMonth();
std::vector<HistoryOrder> getHistoryDateRange(int64_t fromUnix, int64_t toUnix);

Each returns closed orders in that window as HistoryOrder (ticket, symbol, type, lots, open/close price, profit, swap, commission, open/close time) — same struct as MT4Service · History.

auto today = sugar.getHistoryToday();
std::printf("%zu trades closed today\n", today.size());

#include <ctime>
int64_t now = (int64_t)std::time(nullptr);
auto custom = sugar.getHistoryDateRange(now - 30*24*3600, now);   // last 30 days

docs.title: Period profit
docs.text:
double getProfitToday();
double getProfitThisWeek();
double getProfitThisMonth();

Net realized profit (incl. swap & commission) over the window.

std::printf("today %.2f  week %.2f  month %.2f\n",
            sugar.getProfitToday(), sugar.getProfitThisWeek(), sugar.getProfitThisMonth());

docs.title: getDailyStats()
docs.text:
DailyStats getDailyStats();

Today's win/loss summary in one call.

Returns — DailyStats:

Field Type Description totalOrders int Orders closed today winningOrders / losingOrders int Win / loss counts winRate double Winning / total, percent totalProfit double Net profit (incl. swap & commission) bestOrder / worstOrder double Largest win / loss 
DailyStats d = sugar.getDailyStats();
std::printf("Today: %d trades, win rate %.1f%%, net %.2f (best %.2f / worst %.2f)\n",
            d.totalOrders, d.winRate, d.totalProfit, d.bestOrder, d.worstOrder);

Non-trades excluded. Balance/credit history entries are not counted as trades in these aggregates.

docs.title: End-of-day report line
docs.text:
void dailyReport(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    DailyStats d = sugar.getDailyStats();
    std::printf("Today: %d trades | win %.1f%% | net %+.2f | best %+.2f | worst %+.2f\n",
                d.totalOrders, d.winRate, d.totalProfit, d.bestOrder, d.worstOrder);
}

docs.title: Period P/L at a glance
docs.text:
void pnlOverview(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    std::printf("Day %+.2f | Week %+.2f | Month %+.2f\n",
                sugar.getProfitToday(), sugar.getProfitThisWeek(), sugar.getProfitThisMonth());
}

docs.title: Best / worst closed trade this week
docs.text:
void extremes(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    double best = -1e18, worst = 1e18;
    for (const auto& h : sugar.getHistoryThisWeek()) {
        double net = h.profit + h.swap + h.commission;
        best = std::max(best, net); worst = std::min(worst, net);
    }
    std::printf("best %+.2f  worst %+.2f\n", best, worst);
}

docs.title: Realized P/L by symbol (custom range)
docs.text:
#include <map>
#include <ctime>
std::map<std::string,double> pnlBySymbol(MT4Sugar& sugar, int days) {
    int64_t now = (int64_t)std::time(nullptr);
    std::map<std::string,double> m;
    for (const auto& h : sugar.getHistoryDateRange(now - days*24*3600, now))
        m[h.symbol] += h.profit + h.swap + h.commission;
    return m;
}

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 6. Symbols & Risk
docs.text:
Quick symbol facts, plus risk-based position sizing and pre-trade checks. These are the numbers you combine to size and validate an order — MT4 has no server-side orderCheck / orderCalc*, so the sizing helpers compute client-side.

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

docs.title: Symbol information
docs.text:
SymbolInfo getSymbolInfo(const std::string& symbol);    // full params (digits, point, contract, margins, …)
std::vector<std::string> getAllSymbols();               // every symbol name
bool isSymbolAvailable(const std::string& symbol);      // the broker knows this symbol
int  getMinStopLevel(const std::string& symbol);        // min SL/TP distance, in points
int  getSymbolDigits(const std::string& symbol);        // price decimal places

getSymbolInfo returns the SymbolInfo struct — same as MT4Service · Symbols.

if (sugar.isSymbolAvailable("XAUUSD")) {
    int digits = sugar.getSymbolDigits("XAUUSD");
    int minStop = sugar.getMinStopLevel("XAUUSD");
    std::printf("XAUUSD digits=%d  min stop=%d pts\n", digits, minStop);
}

docs.title: Risk & sizing
docs.text:
// Lot size so a stopLossPips stop risks riskPercent% of the balance.
double calculatePositionSize(const std::string& symbol, double riskPercent, double stopLossPips);

// Largest lot the current free margin can open on this symbol.
double getMaxLotSize(const std::string& symbol);

// Can a volume-lot order be opened now? reason explains a false.
bool canOpenOrder(const std::string& symbol, double volume, std::string& reason);

// Margin to open volume lots. MT4 has no margin RPC — estimated from the symbol's
// margin-initial (or contract size / leverage).
double calculateRequiredMargin(const std::string& symbol, double volume);

// Absolute SL/TP prices for a direction ("buy"/"sell") given pip distances from entry.
void calculateSLTP(const std::string& symbol, const std::string& direction, double entryPrice,
                   double stopLossPips, double takeProfitPips, double& slOut, double& tpOut);

// risk 1% of balance on a 20-pip stop
double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", 1.0, 20);
lots = std::min(lots, sugar.getMaxLotSize("EURUSD"));   // cap by free margin

std::string why;
if (!sugar.canOpenOrder("EURUSD", lots, why)) {
    std::printf("cannot open: %s\n", why.c_str());
} else {
    double sl, tp;
    sugar.calculateSLTP("EURUSD", "buy", sugar.getAsk("EURUSD"), 20, 40, sl, tp);
    sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP("EURUSD", lots, sl, tp);
}

calculateRequiredMargin is an estimate (no server margin RPC on MT4): it uses the symbol's marginInitial × volume, else contractSize × volume × price / leverage.

docs.title: Full risk-managed entry
docs.text:
bool safeEntry(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double riskPct, double slPips, double tpPips) {
    double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize(sym, riskPct, slPips);
    lots = std::min(lots, sugar.getMaxLotSize(sym));            // never exceed free margin

    std::string why;
    if (!sugar.canOpenOrder(sym, lots, why)) { std::printf("skip: %s\n", why.c_str()); return false; }

    int ticket = sugar.buyMarketWithPips(sym, lots, slPips, tpPips);
    return ticket != 0;
}

docs.title: Ensure a symbol is tradable before using it
docs.text:
bool ready(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym) {
    if (!sugar.isSymbolAvailable(sym)) { std::printf("%s unknown\n", sym.c_str()); return false; }
    SymbolInfo s = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym);
    return s.tradeMode == 4;                                    // SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL
}

docs.title: Clamp a requested lot to the symbol's grid
docs.text:
double clampLot(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double lots) {
    SymbolInfo s = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym);
    lots = std::max(s.volumeMin, std::min(lots, s.volumeMax));
    if (s.volumeStep > 0) lots = std::round(lots / s.volumeStep) * s.volumeStep;
    return lots;                                                // avoids MQL4 131 (invalid volume)
}

docs.title: Scan all USD pairs the broker offers
docs.text:
#include <vector>
std::vector<std::string> usdPairs(MT4Sugar& sugar) {
    std::vector<std::string> out;
    for (const auto& name : sugar.getAllSymbols())
        if (name.find("USD") != std::string::npos) out.push_back(name);
    return out;
}

docs.title: Estimate margin before committing
docs.text:
if (sugar.calculateRequiredMargin("EURUSD", 1.0) < sugar.getFreeMargin())
    std::puts("1.0 lot is affordable");

Back to: MT4Sugar — Overview

docs.title: MT4Sugar — High-Level One-Liners (Layer 3 of 3)
docs.text:
The shortest path to getting things done: "what's my balance?", "what's the bid?", "buy 0.1 lots", "close everything". Every method is self-contained — no context, no request objects, no protobuf — so prototype code reads like plain English.

Defined in include/metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp + src/mt4_sugar.cpp. The header is protobuf-free and compiles fast.

MT4Sugar (HIGH)    ← you are here — one-liners, pip math, risk sizing
   │ owns
MT4Service (MID)   friendly structs, UTC
   │ owns
MT4Account (LOW)   raw gRPC

Each MT4Sugar owns an MT4Service (and the MT4Account under it). Drop down with sugar.service() for the friendly facade or sugar.account() for raw RPCs.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Orders, not positions. MT4 has no "positions" — getOpenOrders() returns market and pending orders. Sugar talks orders throughout.
  • Never throws on an ordinary rejection. A rejected trade throws ApiError from Layer 1; the sugar helpers catch it and report a false / 0 ticket instead. (A genuine transport failure can still throw TransportError.)
  • Pips. A pip is point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point.
  • UTC by default — times in/out are UTC unless you constructed with utcTimes = false.
#include <metarpc/mt4_sugar.hpp>
using namespace metarpc;

MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");   // or sugar.quickConnect() from env

double lots = sugar.calculatePositionSize("EURUSD", /*risk%*/ 1.0, /*SL pips*/ 20);
int ticket  = sugar.buyMarketWithPips("EURUSD", lots, /*SL*/ 20, /*TP*/ 40);
if (ticket) std::printf("opened #%d\n", ticket);

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrators are small strategy managers built on top of MT4Sugar: they wrap a decision loop (read state → act → repeat) around the one-liner API. A preset coordinates orchestrators behind a single decision. All of them live in examples/demos/ and run from the demos launcher.

Educational examples, not production systems

These orchestrators use deliberately simple heuristics (a trailing offset, a fixed grid, a few account thresholds). They demonstrate the pattern — a strategy built from the SDK — and are templates to build on, not turnkey trading systems. They place small live orders on the demo account and clean up after themselves.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
Each orchestrator is a class that:

  1. takes a connected MT4Sugar& and a small Config in its constructor,
  2. exposes a run() (or execute()) that loops for a bounded number of cycles,
  3. acts through Sugar / Service calls and prints what it does.
class RiskManager {
public:
    struct Config { double maxDrawdownPct{5}; double minMarginLevel{150}; int cycles{5}; };
    RiskManager(metarpc::MT4Sugar& sugar, Config cfg);
    void run();   // read metrics → evaluate limits → act
};

🆚 Orders, not positions. MT4 has no "positions" — these orchestrators manage orders (market + pending in one list). So they use buyMarket / getOrderByTicket / modifyOrderSL / closeOrder / closeAllOrders, not the MT5 *Position* calls.

docs.title: Orchestrators
docs.text:
Each orchestrator has its own page with the annotated class and several worked examples:

# Orchestrator What it does Key Sugar calls 11 Trailing Stop Opens one order, then raises its stop loss as price advances (never lowers it); closes at the end. buyMarket, getBid, modifyOrderSL, closeOrder 13 Grid Trader Lays a symmetric grid of pending orders around price (levels each side, stepPips apart), lists it, then removes it. buyLimit, sellLimit, service().openedOrders, closeOrder 14 Risk Manager Monitors account health each cycle; if drawdown or margin level breaches a limit, it closes everything (kill-switch). getEquity, getMarginLevel, getTotalProfit, closeAllOrders

docs.title: Trailing Stop →
docs.text:
Ride winners, cap the downside. Each cycle reads the bid and, if price advanced, tightens the SL to trailPips behind it — never looser.

double wantSL = bid - trailPips * pip;
if (wantSL > bestSL) { bestSL = wantSL; sugar.modifyOrderSL(ticket, bestSL); }

docs.title: Grid Trader →
docs.text:
Fade a range: buy-limits below price, sell-limits above, levels each side.

for (int i = 1; i <= levels; ++i) {
    sugar.buyLimit (sym, vol, bid - i * stepPips * pip);   // below price
    sugar.sellLimit(sym, vol, ask + i * stepPips * pip);   // above price
}
// … later: sugar.closeOrder(ticket) deletes each pending order.

docs.title: Risk Manager →
docs.text:
A kill-switch: monitor account health and flatten everything on a breach.

double ddPct = (startBalance - sugar.getEquity()) / startBalance * 100.0;
if (ddPct > maxDrawdownPct || (open > 0 && marginLevel > 0 && marginLevel < minMarginLevel))
    sugar.closeAllOrders();   // kill-switch

docs.title: Preset
docs.text:
# Preset What it does 16 Adaptive Market Mode Analyses recent bars, classifies the market (Trending / Ranging / Volatile) and dispatches to the matching orchestrator. 
// analyse last 20 H1 bars → pick a mode → run the right orchestrator
if      (spike > 2.5) demo_risk_manager(sugar, cfg);     // VOLATILE  → defensive
else if (trend > 2.0) demo_trailing_stop(sugar, cfg);    // TRENDING  → ride it
else                  demo_grid_trader(sugar, cfg);      // RANGING   → fade it

docs.title: Orchestrator · Grid Trader
docs.text:
Lay a symmetric grid of pending orders around the current price — buy-limits below, sell-limits above, levels each side — list what went live, then clean the whole grid up. Built on MT4Sugar plus one drop to service().

Source: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_grid_trader.cpp · Run: ./build/demos 13 · API level: HIGH (Sugar) + MID (service())

Educational example

Places small live pending orders on the demo account and deletes them all before returning — nothing is left open. A fixed grid is a template, not a turnkey system.

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
1. Reads bid/ask to centre the grid on price.
  2. For each level i, places a buy-limit i steps below and a sell-limit i steps above.
  3. Drops to service().openedOrders() and counts the live pendings (filter by isPending()).
  4. Deletes every order it placed (closeOrder deletes a pending by ticket).

docs.title: 🧩 The pattern
docs.text:
GridTrader{config} → read bid/ask → place grid (buyLimit/sellLimit each level)
    → list pendings (service().openedOrders filtered by isPending)
    → remove all (closeOrder per ticket)

docs.title: ⚙️ Config
docs.text:
struct Config {
    int    levels{2};        // pending orders on each side
    double stepPips{20.0};   // distance between levels
    double volume{0.01};
};

docs.title: 🏗️ The orchestrator (annotated)
docs.text:
class GridTrader {
public:
    struct Config { int levels{2}; double stepPips{20.0}; double volume{0.01}; };

    GridTrader(MT4Sugar& sugar, std::string symbol, Config cfg)
        : m_s(sugar), m_sym(std::move(symbol)), m_cfg(cfg) {
        m_pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(m_sym).point;
        int d = sugar.getSymbolDigits(m_sym);
        if (d == 3 || d == 5) m_pip *= 10.0;
    }

    void run() {
        double bid = m_s.getBid(m_sym), ask = m_s.getAsk(m_sym);

        // place the grid: a buy-limit i steps below, a sell-limit i steps above
        std::vector<int> tickets;
        for (int i = 1; i <= m_cfg.levels; ++i) {
            double below = bid - i * m_cfg.stepPips * m_pip;   // buy-limit under price
            double above = ask + i * m_cfg.stepPips * m_pip;   // sell-limit over price
            int b = m_s.buyLimit (m_sym, m_cfg.volume, below);
            int s = m_s.sellLimit(m_sym, m_cfg.volume, above);
            if (b) tickets.push_back(b);
            if (s) tickets.push_back(s);
        }
        if (tickets.empty()) return;            // market closed / too close to price

        // count the live pendings via the mid-level facade
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(600));
        int pending = 0;
        for (const auto& o : m_s.service().openedOrders())
            if (o.isPending()) ++pending;

        // clean up: delete everything we placed
        for (int t : tickets) m_s.closeOrder(t);  // closeOrder deletes a pending by ticket
    }
private:
    MT4Sugar& m_s; std::string m_sym; double m_pip{0}; Config m_cfg;
};

Key calls: getBid / getAsk · buyLimit / sellLimit · service().openedOrders() + Order::isPending() · closeOrder.

🆚 MT4: pending and market orders share one list — service().openedOrders() returns both, so filter with o.isPending(). The same closeOrder(ticket) deletes a pending or closes a market order.

docs.title: 1) Run it with defaults
docs.text:
MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

GridTrader gt(sugar, "EURUSD", GridTrader::Config{});
gt.run();   // places 2 levels/side, lists, removes

docs.title: 2) A wider, denser grid
docs.text:
GridTrader::Config cfg;
cfg.levels   = 5;       // 5 orders each side (10 total)
cfg.stepPips = 30;      // spaced 30 pips apart
cfg.volume   = 0.02;
GridTrader(sugar, "EURUSD", cfg).run();

docs.title: 3) Leave the grid live (don't auto-clean)
docs.text:
The demo removes its grid; a real strategy keeps it and reacts to fills. Just place and return:

std::vector<int> placeGrid(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym,
                           int levels, double stepPips, double vol) {
    double point = sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym).point;
    double pip = (sugar.getSymbolDigits(sym) % 2 == 1) ? point * 10 : point;
    double bid = sugar.getBid(sym), ask = sugar.getAsk(sym);
    std::vector<int> tickets;
    for (int i = 1; i <= levels; ++i) {
        if (int b = sugar.buyLimit (sym, vol, bid - i * stepPips * pip)) tickets.push_back(b);
        if (int s = sugar.sellLimit(sym, vol, ask + i * stepPips * pip)) tickets.push_back(s);
    }
    return tickets;   // caller decides when to closeOrder() them
}

docs.title: 4) One-sided grid (buy-limits only)
docs.text:
for (int i = 1; i <= levels; ++i)
    sugar.buyLimit("EURUSD", 0.01, bid - i * stepPips * pip);   // accumulate on dips

docs.title: 5) Remove only this symbol's pendings
docs.text:
int removeGrid(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym) {
    int n = 0;
    for (const auto& o : sugar.getOrdersBySymbol(sym))
        if (o.isPending() && sugar.closeOrder(o.ticket)) ++n;
    return n;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Too close to price. A limit/stop inside the broker's getMinStopLevel is rejected — buyLimit/sellLimit return 0. Keep stepPips comfortably above the minimum.
  • One shared list. openedOrders() includes any market orders too — always filter by isPending() before treating a row as a grid order.
  • Fills turn pending → market. If a limit triggers, that ticket becomes a market order; closeOrder still handles it, but it's no longer "pending".
  • Clean up. The demo deletes every ticket it placed; if you keep the grid, track the tickets yourself.

docs.title: Orchestrator · Risk Manager
docs.text:
A monitoring orchestrator — a kill-switch. Each cycle it reads account health (equity, margin level, floating P/L, open orders); if drawdown or margin level breaches a limit, it closes everything. On a healthy/flat account it just reports. Built entirely on MT4Sugar.

Source: examples/demos/orchestrators/14_risk_manager.cpp · Run: ./build/demos 14 · API level: HIGH (Sugar)

Read-only unless a limit breaks

This orchestrator opens nothing. It only reads metrics — and acts just once, by flattening all orders, if a guard rail is crossed. Safe to run on any account.

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
1. Captures the start balance.
  2. Each cycle reads equity, margin level, floating P/L and the open-order count.
  3. Computes drawdown % from the start balance.
  4. Breach? (drawdown > maxDrawdownPct or open > 0 && 0 < marginLevel < minMarginLevel) → closeAllOrders() and stop.

docs.title: 🧩 The pattern
docs.text:
RiskManager{config} → run(cycles):
    read equity / marginLevel / floatP&L / openCount
    ddPct = (startBalance - equity) / startBalance * 100
    if ddPct > maxDrawdownPct OR (open>0 && marginLevel in (0, minMarginLevel)):
        closeAllOrders()   → break
    → repeat

docs.title: ⚙️ Config
docs.text:
struct Config {
    double maxDrawdownPct{5.0};    // flatten if equity is this % below the start balance
    double minMarginLevel{150.0};  // ... or if the margin level drops below this %
    int    cycles{5};
    int    intervalMs{800};
};

docs.title: 🏗️ The orchestrator (annotated)
docs.text:
class RiskManager {
public:
    struct Config { double maxDrawdownPct{5.0}; double minMarginLevel{150.0}; int cycles{5}; int intervalMs{800}; };

    RiskManager(MT4Sugar& sugar, Config cfg) : m_s(sugar), m_cfg(cfg) {
        m_startBalance = sugar.getBalance();      // baseline for drawdown
    }

    void run() {
        for (int c = 1; c <= m_cfg.cycles; ++c) {
            double equity      = m_s.getEquity();        // balance + floating P/L
            double marginLevel = m_s.getMarginLevel();   // percent (0 when flat)
            double floating    = m_s.getTotalProfit();   // summed floating P/L
            int    open        = m_s.countOpenOrders();  // live orders
            double ddPct = m_startBalance > 0
                         ? (m_startBalance - equity) / m_startBalance * 100.0 : 0.0;

            bool breach = (ddPct > m_cfg.maxDrawdownPct) ||
                          (open > 0 && marginLevel > 0 && marginLevel < m_cfg.minMarginLevel);
            if (breach) {
                int closed = m_s.closeAllOrders();       // ⚠ kill-switch: flatten everything
                (void)closed;
                break;
            }
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(m_cfg.intervalMs));
        }
    }
private:
    MT4Sugar& m_s; Config m_cfg; double m_startBalance{0};
};

Key Sugar calls: getBalance (baseline) · getEquity · getMarginLevel · getTotalProfit · countOpenOrders · closeAllOrders.

🆚 MT4: the kill-switch is closeAllOrders() — it closes market orders and deletes pendings (MT4's one order list). getMarginLevel() is 0 when nothing is open, so the margin test guards on open > 0 && marginLevel > 0.

docs.title: 1) Run it with defaults
docs.text:
MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

RiskManager rm(sugar, RiskManager::Config{});
rm.run();   // monitors 5 cycles; flattens on a breach

docs.title: 2) Stricter limits, longer watch
docs.text:
RiskManager::Config cfg;
cfg.maxDrawdownPct = 2.0;     // tighter drawdown cap
cfg.minMarginLevel = 300.0;   // demand more headroom
cfg.cycles         = 60;      // watch longer
cfg.intervalMs     = 1000;
RiskManager(sugar, cfg).run();

docs.title: 3) One-shot health check (no loop)
docs.text:
bool breached(MT4Sugar& sugar, double startBalance, double maxDDpct, double minMargin) {
    double ddPct = (startBalance - sugar.getEquity()) / startBalance * 100.0;
    double ml = sugar.getMarginLevel();
    int open = sugar.countOpenOrders();
    return ddPct > maxDDpct || (open > 0 && ml > 0 && ml < minMargin);
}

docs.title: 4) Daily-loss kill-switch
docs.text:
Flatten when today's realized + floating loss exceeds a cash cap:

double todaysPnL = sugar.getProfitToday() + sugar.getTotalProfit();  // realized + floating
if (todaysPnL < -200.0) {                                            // -$200 daily stop
    int closed = sugar.closeAllOrders();
    std::printf("daily stop hit — closed %d\n", closed);
}

docs.title: 5) Per-symbol guard instead of account-wide
docs.text:
void capSymbol(MT4Sugar& sugar, const std::string& sym, double maxLoss) {
    if (sugar.getProfitBySymbol(sym) < -maxLoss)
        sugar.closeAllBySymbol(sym);     // flatten just this instrument
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Margin level is 0 when flat. Always pair the margin test with open > 0 && marginLevel > 0, or a flat account reads as a breach.
  • Each getter is a round-trip. getEquity / getMarginLevel / … each fetch a fresh summary; for many figures at once read getAccountInfo() once.
  • Kill-switch is total. closeAllOrders() flattens everything, including orders other strategies placed. Scope it (e.g. closeAllBySymbol) if you share the account.
  • Drawdown baseline. It's measured against the start balance captured in the constructor — reconstruct the object to reset the baseline.

docs.title: Orchestrator · Trailing Stop
docs.text:
Open one order, then ratchet its stop loss up as price advances — never down. The classic "let winners run, cap the downside" manager, built entirely on MT4Sugar.

Source: examples/demos/orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.cpp · Run: ./build/demos 11 · API level: HIGH (Sugar)

Educational example

Places a small live 0.01 BUY on the demo account and closes it before returning. The heuristic (a fixed pip trail) is a template to build on, not a turnkey system.

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
1. Opens a market BUY.
  2. Each cycle, reads the bid and computes a stop trailPips behind it.
  3. Raises the SL only if the new level is higher than the current one (monotonic ratchet).
  4. Closes the order at the end of the run.

docs.title: 🧩 The pattern
docs.text:
TrailingStop{config} → buyMarket → run(cycles):
    read bid → wantSL = bid - trailPips·pip → if wantSL > bestSL: raise SL → repeat
→ closeOrder

docs.title: ⚙️ Config
docs.text:
struct Config {
    double trailPips{20.0};   // keep the SL this many pips behind the best bid
    int    cycles{8};         // how many times to re-evaluate
    int    intervalMs{700};   // pause between cycles
};

docs.title: 🏗️ The orchestrator (annotated)
docs.text:
class TrailingStop {
public:
    struct Config { double trailPips{20.0}; int cycles{8}; int intervalMs{700}; };

    TrailingStop(MT4Sugar& sugar, std::string symbol, double volume, Config cfg)
        : m_s(sugar), m_sym(std::move(symbol)), m_vol(volume), m_cfg(cfg) {
        // pip = point, scaled ×10 on 3/5-digit symbols (so "pips" means what a trader means)
        m_pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(m_sym).point;
        int d = sugar.getSymbolDigits(m_sym);
        if (d == 3 || d == 5) m_pip *= 10.0;
    }

    void run() {
        int ticket = m_s.buyMarket(m_sym, m_vol);
        if (ticket == 0) return;                 // rejected (market closed?) — nothing to trail

        double bestSL = 0;
        for (int c = 1; c <= m_cfg.cycles; ++c) {
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(m_cfg.intervalMs));

            bool found = false;
            Order o = m_s.getOrderByTicket(ticket, found);
            if (!found) return;                  // closed elsewhere — stop managing it

            double bid    = m_s.getBid(m_sym);
            double wantSL = bid - m_cfg.trailPips * m_pip;
            if (wantSL > bestSL) {               // only ever tighten
                bestSL = wantSL;
                m_s.modifyOrderSL(ticket, bestSL);
            }
        }
        m_s.closeOrder(ticket);
    }
private:
    MT4Sugar& m_s; std::string m_sym; double m_vol, m_pip{0}; Config m_cfg;
};

Key Sugar calls: buyMarket · getSymbolInfo / getSymbolDigits (pip sizing) · getBid · getOrderByTicket · modifyOrderSL · closeOrder.

🆚 MT4: buyMarket returns an int ticket (0 = rejected, never throws), and trailing works on an order via modifyOrderSL / getOrderByTicket — MT4 has no separate "position" object.

docs.title: 1) Run it with defaults
docs.text:
MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

TrailingStop ts(sugar, "EURUSD", 0.01, TrailingStop::Config{});
ts.run();   // opens, trails for 8 cycles, closes

docs.title: 2) A tighter, faster trail
docs.text:
TrailingStop::Config cfg;
cfg.trailPips  = 10;    // hug price closer
cfg.cycles     = 30;    // manage longer
cfg.intervalMs = 400;   // check more often
TrailingStop(sugar, "EURUSD", 0.02, cfg).run();

docs.title: 3) Trail an existing order instead of opening one
docs.text:
The demo opens its own trade; in a real strategy you often already hold one. The core is just the ratchet — apply it to any ticket:

void trailExisting(MT4Sugar& sugar, int ticket, double trailPips, int cycles) {
    bool found = false;
    Order o0 = sugar.getOrderByTicket(ticket, found);
    if (!found) return;
    double pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(o0.symbol).point;
    int d = sugar.getSymbolDigits(o0.symbol);
    if (d == 3 || d == 5) pip *= 10.0;          // 3/5-digit → ×10

    double bestSL = o0.stopLoss;
    for (int c = 0; c < cycles; ++c) {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
        bool ok = false; Order o = sugar.getOrderByTicket(ticket, ok);
        if (!ok) return;
        double wantSL = sugar.getBid(o.symbol) - trailPips * pip;
        if (wantSL > bestSL) { bestSL = wantSL; sugar.modifyOrderSL(ticket, bestSL); }
    }
}

docs.title: 4) Break-even first, then trail
docs.text:
Lock the stop at entry once in profit, then start trailing:

bool found = false;
Order o = sugar.getOrderByTicket(ticket, found);
double pip = sugar.getSymbolInfo(o.symbol).point * 10.0;   // 5-digit FX

if (found && sugar.getBid(o.symbol) > o.openPrice + 10 * pip) {
    sugar.modifyOrderSL(ticket, o.openPrice);              // break-even
    // ... then run the trail loop from example 3 ...
}

docs.title: 5) Respect the broker's minimum stop distance
docs.text:
A stop too close to price is rejected (ApiError 130). Clamp the trail to getMinStopLevel:

double point   = sugar.getSymbolInfo("EURUSD").point;
double pip      = point * 10.0;
double minDist  = sugar.getMinStopLevel("EURUSD") * point;
double trail    = std::max(20 * pip, minDist);             // never closer than the broker allows
double wantSL   = sugar.getBid("EURUSD") - trail;

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Only raises the SL. By design it never loosens the stop — a reversal just hits the last locked level.
  • BUY-only demo. The example trails a long; for shorts, mirror it (getAsk, wantSL = ask + trail, only ever lower the SL).
  • Min stop distance. Too tight a trailPips → modifyOrderSL returns false (MQL4 130, see example 5).
  • Order may vanish. getOrderByTicket(found=false) means it was closed elsewhere (TP hit, manual close) — the loop bails out cleanly.

docs.title: Preset · Adaptive Market Mode
docs.text:
A preset coordinates orchestrators behind one decision. This one reads recent price action, classifies the market, and dispatches to the matching orchestrator:

  • TRENDING → Trailing Stop — ride the move
  • RANGING → Grid Trader — fade the range
  • VOLATILE → Risk Manager — defensive / kill-switch

Source: examples/demos/presets/16_adaptive_preset.cpp · Run: ./build/demos 16 · API level: MID (service().lastBars) + HIGH (orchestrators)

Educational example

The classifier is a two-number heuristic over 20 H1 bars. It demonstrates routing a decision to the right strategy — it is not a market regime model. Whatever it dispatches runs on the demo account and cleans up after itself.

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
1. Pulls the last 20 H1 bars via service().lastBars (MT4 timeframes are in minutes — Timeframe::H1 == 60).
  2. Computes two ratios from the bars:
  3. trend = net directional move ÷ average bar range (how far price travelled in "average ranges"),
  4. spike = biggest bar range ÷ average range (how outsized the largest bar was).
  5. Classifies: spike > 2.5 → VOLATILE; else trend > 2.0 → TRENDING; else RANGING.
  6. Dispatches to the matching orchestrator.

docs.title: 🧩 The pattern
docs.text:
AdaptiveMarketModePreset → analyse(last 20 H1 bars):
    avgRange, maxRange, netMove
    trend = netMove / avgRange ;  spike = maxRange / avgRange
    spike>2.5 → VOLATILE ; trend>2.0 → TRENDING ; else RANGING
→ dispatch: VOLATILE→RiskManager · TRENDING→TrailingStop · RANGING→GridTrader

docs.title: 🏗️ The preset (annotated)
docs.text:
enum class MarketMode { Trending, Ranging, Volatile };

class AdaptiveMarketModePreset {
public:
    AdaptiveMarketModePreset(MT4Sugar& sugar, std::string symbol)
        : m_s(sugar), m_sym(std::move(symbol)) {}

    MarketMode analyse() {
        // drop to the mid-level facade for OHLC bars (timeframe in MINUTES: H1 == 60)
        auto bars = m_s.service().lastBars(m_sym, Timeframe::H1, 20);
        if (bars.size() < 5) return MarketMode::Ranging;    // not enough data → neutral

        double sumRange = 0, maxRange = 0;
        for (const auto& b : bars) {
            double r = b.high - b.low;
            sumRange += r;
            maxRange = std::max(maxRange, r);
        }
        double avgRange = sumRange / bars.size();
        double move  = std::fabs(bars.back().close - bars.front().close);  // net move
        double trend = avgRange > 0 ? move / avgRange : 0;                 // in "ranges"
        double spike = avgRange > 0 ? maxRange / avgRange : 1;             // biggest vs typical

        if (spike > 2.5) return MarketMode::Volatile;       // an outsized bar → defensive
        if (trend > 2.0) return MarketMode::Trending;       // strong directional drift
        return MarketMode::Ranging;
    }

    void execute(const Config& cfg) {
        switch (analyse()) {                                // dispatch to one orchestrator
            case MarketMode::Trending: demo_trailing_stop(m_s, cfg); break;
            case MarketMode::Ranging:  demo_grid_trader(m_s, cfg);   break;
            case MarketMode::Volatile: demo_risk_manager(m_s, cfg);  break;
        }
    }
private:
    MT4Sugar& m_s; std::string m_sym;
};

Key calls: service().lastBars(symbol, Timeframe::H1, 20) → classify → call one of demo_trailing_stop / demo_grid_trader / demo_risk_manager.

🆚 MT4: Timeframe values are minute counts (H1 = 60, D1 = 1440); lastBars supplies the required start time for you.

docs.title: 1) Run it
docs.text:
MT4Sugar sugar("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443);
sugar.connect(1235959737, "password", "EGlobal-Demo");

AdaptiveMarketModePreset preset(sugar, "EURUSD");
preset.execute(Config{});   // analyse → pick a mode → run the matching orchestrator

docs.title: 2) Just the classification (no trading)
docs.text:
MarketMode mode = AdaptiveMarketModePreset(sugar, "EURUSD").analyse();
// route it yourself, log it, or gate another decision on it

docs.title: 3) Tune the thresholds
docs.text:
The cutoffs are the knobs. Make it quicker to call "trending", slower to call "volatile":

// in analyse():
if (spike > 3.0) return MarketMode::Volatile;   // only a very big bar = volatile
if (trend > 1.5) return MarketMode::Trending;   // call trends sooner
return MarketMode::Ranging;

docs.title: 4) Use a different timeframe / lookback
docs.text: auto bars = sugar.service().lastBars("EURUSD", Timeframe::M15, 48);   // last 12h of M15

docs.title: 5) Add a fourth mode (quiet → do nothing)
docs.text:
if (trend < 0.5 && spike < 1.5) return MarketMode::Ranging;   // treat "quiet" as skip
// ... and in execute(), map that case to a no-op instead of placing a grid.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Heuristic, not a model. Two ratios over 20 bars is a demo classifier — validate before trusting it with size.
  • Timeframe is minutes. Pass Timeframe::H1 (not a raw 4 / index) — that's the low-level quoteHistory enum, a different scheme.
  • Needs history. Fewer than 5 bars → it defaults to RANGING. Thin symbols / fresh connections may return less than you ask for.
  • Dispatch inherits the orchestrator's risk. Whatever it routes to places live demo orders — the preset is only as safe as the orchestrator it picks.
